entries.summary: New Panel: a readable message when something is missing, an optional picture prompt, and panels without a picture now say Not drawn yet.
entries.detail: Testers, 2026-11-09. The New Panel window's message is now light red and bold (it was dark red on near-black), and the box it is about is outlined. On I'll write it myself the picture prompt is optional: left empty, what you wrote in What happens here? is used. A panel with no picture yet reads Not drawn yet where it read Unknown (it is drawn in the version's art style like every panel). Write it for me now names in the picture prompt only the characters your line names, or exactly the ones you picked, so no one extra is drawn.

entries.summary: New Panel's window is simpler: characters, assets and prominence as on every panel, and no picture step.
entries.detail: The New Panel window now uses the same + Add character and + Add asset picker as every panel, adds Prominence (Minimize, Default or Maximize), and no longer asks about the picture: the panel lands, and Replace, Regen or Generate Images give it one there.

entries.summary: New Panel: add a picture panel anywhere in your story, right after the one you choose.
entries.detail: Under each box on the Story panels (and on each Review row), New Panel adds a picture panel right after it; never after the Closing. Say what happens there (kept as the panel's Narrative Outline), pick its characters and assets, then Write it for me (1 token: title, picture prompt, shape and the panel's story text) or write it yourself, and take its picture from the Archive, generate it, or leave it for later. Your plan's panel limit applies. Generate Story starts over and does not keep added panels.

entries.summary: Video: Retouch a finished take, as a Small fix or a Bigger change; the result is a new take.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "Is there a way to Retouch a video that is already built?"; "we are going to need a retouch for sure so build it. Then we can refine it as needed." Spec claude/VIDEO_TAKE_RETOUCH_SPEC.md. A Retouch button on every finished take opens a window: the take, What do you want to change?, the shot's references that have a picture (tick to use), and How big a change?: Small fix (fal-ai/kling-video/o1/standard/video-to-video/edit, keep_audio on: keeps the motion and the sound; takes of 3 to 10 s; up to 4 references; $0.126 a second) or Bigger change (bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-video with the take as @Video1, generate_audio as the take; length snapped to 4/5/6/8/10/12/15 s; up to 8 references; priced on input plus output seconds). The price shows before sending. The result is a new take ("Take 2 - retouched from take 1") made through the same fal queue, webhook and sweep as every take; the pinned take stays pinned; it counts toward the shot's 10; it is out of date when its source is. Refused: a take not finished, a shot already making a take or at 10 takes, a length outside the size's range, no words; references are re-checked on the server. takes gains source_take_id, retouch_text, retouch_kind. Debug Mode logs the full input.

entries.summary: Video: voices from off-screen stay off the faces on screen; 10 takes a shot; takes across the shot.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08, takes 11-13: a line ticked off-screen was still said by Gubuk on screen; a line with no name drew a second Gubuk to say it; "Let's lift the limit on 3 takes"; "put the viewer below the Left hand side as well. To make more room for multiple". The take that worked (episode 1 take 3) wrote the line as something Gubuk hears: "Gubuk hears Drel yelling in the distance". The script now does the same: "As this happens, Gubuk hears Drel calling from off-screen, in the distance: '...' (Drel is not in this shot)." ("we hear" when no one is on screen); a line with no name is such a voice, never "Someone says". Then each character on screen with no line "does not speak; his mouth stays closed", and "No one on screen speaks." when no one on screen has a line. A speaker only heard off-screen is not sent as a reference picture, is not offered by the named-but-not-in-References hint, and what a line says no longer names anyone ("Where is Emanon?"); a speaker also seen doing something in the shot keeps their picture. A line with no Who is warned. The leave-and-return warning ignores a voice heard off-screen and an end that has them gone. Takes: 10 a shot (was 3); the takes and Generate take sit in a row across the whole shot under both halves. Director's Notes: the start names what lies around (bodies, fallen weapons, props) and every line names its speaker.

entries.summary: Retouch can flip a picture left to right; a video keyframe's Retouch uses its shot's references; the Director's buttons are filled with their price.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "Add an Option to the retouch drop down to flip the image from left to right... basically mirror image it. It should work also in storyboard"; "when you open the retouch on a key Frame image in a shot... The references in that shot should show in the the Retouch modal to use" ("only the Shots References. They can add more and open again"); "Put the (1 token) on the buttons themselves... Fill these buttons in with yellow... Just like our Generate Story button". Flip: a new first choice in Retouch's What are you changing? menu, on story panels and video keyframes (not Image Builder pictures). The server mirrors the picture with no AI and no tokens; the copy keeps the source's rights verdict. A story panel's old picture goes into its Revert slot as a retouch's does (owner, lock, title-panel, busy and rights checks as on Retouch; the picture leaving the slot is released); a keyframe's every copy in the episode takes the flip with the old one in Revert. The words box hides and the button reads Flip image. Keyframe Retouch: the reference menu lists the shot's References that have a picture; the server re-checks them and sends them in place of the panel's (Expand sends none). The Director's buttons are btn-primary, with (n tokens) on the button, level with the Style menu.

entries.summary: Video: the Director - Create Shots plans the cuts; Director's Notes writes every shot's direction.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "we need to have two separate buttons at the top. 1. Create Cuts... 2. Build the Shot list... Then the AI can do the Shot list knowing what the cuts are"; "lets start the concept of our AI Director... like our AI Editor on books"; "Directors Notes!". The single Write / Rewrite the shot list button becomes two, each with its price and tooltip. Create Shots: the Director reads the pictures in story order and divides them into shots of one to five pictures, named; nothing else is written. A planned shot with exactly the pictures of a shot already there is that shot and keeps its name, words, references, cut style and takes; other shots start empty, and shots that no longer exist go with their takes and files (asked first whenever there is more than one shot or any takes). The overall direction is not touched. Director's Notes: the Director sees the shots as they stand (SHOT n headers and CUT markers) and writes the overall direction and every box of every shot; the cuts never move, a name given by hand is kept, the references become the characters named, and takes stay, marked out of date. Pressed on an episode that is one shot of more than five pictures, it asks "This episode isn't cut yet. Create Shots first?" and then runs both. Progress and confirm wording speaks of the Director. Jobs record which button (episode_writer_jobs.kind); Create Shots is charged as video_shot_plan.

entries.summary: Video: each shot is laid out in two halves, with its own character and asset references.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "Divide the shot panel into two horizontal halves... each question on its own accordion panel on the left... On the right half the pictures from left to right... the Shot duration up on the same line with the shot's name... the small cut here button between each image... the generate take button on the bottom of the right half"; "add the ability to add character and asset references... and see the references that are already on that shot... just like the Review tab, Storyboard and Image builder". Top line: Shot n, its name, How long? (4-15 s). Across the shot: References, Characters and Assets as chips (click to see, x to remove), + Add character / + Add asset pickers, how many of the 9 pictures go, and a hint with Add when a character with a picture is named in the words but not referenced (assets are added by hand). Left: one fold-out panel per question (start, what the characters do, what they say, camera, end, sound and surroundings); a closed panel shows its words greyed and its warnings as a count; shot-wide warnings sit above them. Right: the pictures left to right with a small round cut button in each gap, then the takes and Generate take. On a narrow screen the right half comes first. References are saved per shot and are exactly what a reference take sends (an asset is named as a thing that must look like its picture); a shot never given references starts from the characters named in its words; the shot list writer fills each shot's characters; Cut here keeps them on both shots and UnCut joins them; Copy carries them; changing them marks takes out of date. Replaces v3.5.21's folded Words line and the Also sent line.

entries.summary: Video: each shot's words fold into one line until opened.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "you gotta figure out a way so the prompts don't take up so much space. Maybe an accordion inside the shot panel." Under a shot's pictures, one line: Words, the start and the end shortened (start -> end), the number of actions and lines, the length, and how many warnings it has. A click opens the shot's boxes (warnings first, then the boxes); another folds them. Each shot opens on its own and stays as left while the page is open; shots are folded when an episode opens and after the shot list is written. Generate take stays visible on a folded shot. The open boxes are tighter: one line each until typed into, growing as you type.

entries.summary: Video: Write the shot list plans the cuts and fills every box; pictures in a shot can be archived.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "have it do the cuts then put the prompts in"; "the Rewrite shot list should basically start over and clear what's there"; "we need to give them the ability to Archive pics from the KeyFrames". Write the shot list now sees every picture of the episode in order and plans the shots itself (runs of 1 to 5 pictures, cut where the place changes, time jumps or someone must leave and come back), names them, and fills each shot's start, actions, lines (who, during which action, off-screen), camera, end, sounds, surroundings and length. It starts over every time: the episode's shots are replaced (pictures keep their order, sources and Revert slots); if the episode has takes it says how many will be deleted and asks first, and it waits while a shot is being made. A plan that skips, repeats or reorders a picture, or puts more than 5 in a shot, changes nothing and charges nothing. Each picture card has Archive: the exact picture (retouched or not) is copied into the campaign's Archive as '<panel title> (video)' in the version's art style, with the archive cap and rights check; pressed again by its archiver it comes out. The Tall/Square picture tags and Expand no longer show on reference models.

entries.summary: Video: each shot is described in plain-word boxes, and reference mode is the default.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "instead of one prompt break it up into things users understand" (claude/VIDEO_REFERENCE_SHOTS_SPEC.md). Each shot has one set of boxes instead of a box per picture: How does the shot start? / What do the characters do? (numbered) / What do they say? (who, the line, When, heard off-screen) / What does the camera do? / How does the shot end? / How long? (4 to 15 s), with sounds and surroundings under a toggle. Under the pictures: who is also sent as a character picture, and who cannot be and why. Plain-word checks warn about an action in the wrong box, someone who leaves and is needed again, too much for the length, more than 5 pictures, a line with no When, and no end. The server joins the boxes into one script: the named cast's pictures first (they win), the first picture as the opening, later pictures for place only (no poses), then start, actions with their lines, camera, end, sound, surroundings. Seedance 2.0 Fast (reference) is the default; the keyframe models are grouped as Keyframes (exact frames) and get the same script on every move. Old per-picture words show as the shot's actions until saved. The shot list writer fills the boxes from its answer until v3.5.20 writes them box by box.

entries.summary: Video: debug mode shows what each Generate sends.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08, after two takes meant as reference tests came back as keyframe takes: "Put what you need to see in debug mode." Each Generate writes one line: the episode's model and whether that is REFERENCE or KEYFRAME mode, each move's length, pictures and full words, the cast sent, and every character of the version with its reference picture and why one is not usable (none saved, or not a Campaignia picture). A save that changes the model says so (old -> new), and opening the Video tab lists the models the server offers.

entries.summary: Video: the pin (as on the version picker and My Campaigns) replaces the stars on episodes and takes.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "Shouldnt we replace the stars with our SOP Pins?" The episode row, the Pin this episode button and each take now use _vpickPinSvg: filled when pinned, outline when not. A pinned take is the one the shot uses in the episode (Pinned: the take this shot uses in the episode / Pin this take: use it in the episode); one per shot, as the star was. The episode box says 'pinned take(s)' where it said 'chosen'.

entries.summary: Video: two test models, Seedance 2.0 Reference and Seedance 2.0 Fast Reference, that make each shot as one clip directed from references instead of fixed keyframes.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08, after a take where Gubuk doubled and changed between two keyframes: 'Let's just try reference option... hard code that in for a second and let me test it.' With a Reference model chosen, a shot is one clip on fal's Seedance 2.0 reference-to-video: its first 5 keyframes (in order) and the reference pictures of the cast named in the shot's words or the overall direction (the version's own picture, else the character's; 9 pictures at most) are sent as @Image1... with words that name each one, then the boxes in order. Its length is the boxes' lengths added up, 4 to 15 seconds. The clip does not start or end exactly on the keyframes. Prices shown are the image-to-video ones until fal's are read.

entries.summary: Video: shots can be named; a shot keeps at most 3 takes; the cut sits on the top border of the shot below it.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: "We do need the name on the shot"; "for now we limit them to 3 takes"; the UnCut button "right on the top border of the shot... So you know you mean the shot below the line"; Delete "actually deletes the take... no retrieval". Each shot has a name box beside its number (one line, up to 120 characters; saved with the episode, kept by Copy; a new shot from Cut here starts unnamed, UnCut keeps the first shot's name). At 3 takes Generate take is closed with '3 takes max - delete one to make another'; the server refuses a 4th before anything is sent to fal, and Generate all shots skips full shots and names them. The cut label and UnCut sit in the middle of the lower shot's top border; the dashed line between shots is gone. Delete take (unchanged) asks, then removes the take, its moves and their files from storage.

entries.summary: Video: every clip is made wide (16:9); a square or tall keyframe is flagged with Expand, and Generate warns before making a shot that has one.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: a wide title picture and a tall Gubuk made a nearly square take; 'go with... whatever most non phone videos are made in now'; 'Option 1' (Expand); 'Generate should stop and ask and warn.' Every model that takes a shape is asked for 16:9 (Kling takes its shape from the picture). A keyframe under 1.25 wide-to-tall (square or tall; ordinary 4:3 panels pass) shows 'Tall picture: the video is wide' with Expand: one retouch that redraws it wide in its art style, the episode's copy only, with Revert. Generate take and Generate all shots name such pictures and ask: Cancel or Generate anyway.

entries.summary: Video: a shot's takes sit at its foot, under the keyframes, with Generate take at the right of that row.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'The viewer should appear under the key frame images... down near the button.' The shot's title line stays at the top.

entries.summary: Video: each picture and the box to its right sit in one unit with a thin light border, two units to a row; keyframes open bigger on click.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'I want it obvious they are locked together. Unlike the storyboard panels.' Pictures and boxes a little smaller so two pairs fit a row (one on a narrow window); each box as tall as its picture. Clicking a keyframe opens it bigger, as on the Storyboard.

entries.summary: Video: Generate take sits at each shot's bottom right, after its last panel.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'Put the generate take button at the end of the take... bottom right corner.' The shot's title and its takes stay at the top.

entries.summary: Video: moving pictures or Cut here no longer hides a box's words; a keyframe retouch uses the version's art style.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: moving panels or Cut here lost the prompt text (v3.5.07 put a box's words aside when its keyframe's role changed). Now a box belongs to the picture on its left and always keeps its words: Cut here leaves it in the shot it was cut from, as that shot's After box, and the new shot starts on the next picture; UnCut makes it the move to the next picture again; a moved picture takes its box with it. Ian: 'pass the current art style to the image that is getting retouched... of the version the episode is on': the version's own art style, else its session's, else the campaign's.

entries.summary: Video: Retouch and Revert on every keyframe. Only the episode's copy changes; the storyboard is not touched.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'put the retouch option on the keyframes'. The Story panels' Retouch window (markers, picked reference) on a keyframe; a keyframe from the storyboard brings that panel's cast and assets as references, one from the Archive its own shape and style. The usual retouch price, spent when the picture arrives, through the shared picture pipeline (routes/images.js: startKeyframeRetouch and a 'keyframe' webhook branch). Every keyframe of the episode showing the old picture takes the new one, with the old in a one-step Revert slot (free). Takes made from the old picture show out of date.

entries.summary: Video: odd shots now clearly greyer than even ones.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'I'm not seeing any differences in the background color of the odd and even shots.' The page background showed through the shot boxes and drowned the v3.5.07 shading; the boxes are more solid now and odd shots carry a clear grey wash.

entries.summary: Video: the last keyframe of a shot gets an optional After box (what happens after that picture until the cut); UnCut - Join with previous shot; odd shots shaded; Generate take and Generate all shots.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: Gubuk hears Drel, looks around and runs off after his keyframe and before the cut. When the After box has words, the shot gets one more move that starts on that picture with no end picture; empty, nothing changes. The shot list writer may write an after move (from the last keyframe) and may give a voice from off screen ('Drel (off-screen)'). A keyframe's words follow its role, so Cut here puts the move words aside and UnCut brings them back. A change that would delete a shot's takes now shows the result behind its question.

entries.summary: Orphaned pictures and PDFs now splits orphaned into ready to move (what Move to holding would take now) and waiting (younger than the move's 30 days; print PDFs 90).
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'if they are too new shouldn't they be in the Too New column?' The report calls a file orphaned after a day; the move waits 30 days. A headline line (ready / waiting), two new columns, a moves column on the oldest 200 and in the CSV (next move, from a date, or never for a file put back before). The keep list is read the same way the move reads it. The move itself is unchanged.

entries.summary: Write the shot list no longer fails on a long shot: the writer is told every move by name, and its answer is lined up by the keyframe each move starts on.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'The shot list came back incomplete (shot 1 came back with 16 moves, not 15)'. A shot of 16 keyframes has 15 moves; the writer added one from the last keyframe. Each move now says which keyframe it starts on ('from'); a move from the last keyframe, or a second move from the same one, is dropped. Without 'from', one too many loses the last. A missing move still fails the list, and nothing is charged.

entries.summary: The Video tab is rebuilt as Episodes: an episode is shots joined by cuts; a shot is one continuous camera run through one or more keyframes; each shot can have several takes, one chosen.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: 'Episode is made up of Shots... Each Shot can have multiple takes... Between each shot we should have a Cut'. New tables episodes, shots, keyframes, takes, moves and episode_writer_jobs; the old video tables are dropped once on first start (marker video_old_tables_dropped; Ian: no data to keep). Cut here splits a shot, Join removes a cut; Make this shot makes a take; the episode video joins the chosen takes with plain cuts. A one-keyframe shot brings that picture to life. The shot list writer is told where the cuts are. Saves go one at a time and the server locks the episode while it saves (the doubled-pictures bug). Cut styles, Final Cut and the Archive come in later builds.

entries.summary: The account menu sits further right (16px from the edge); the admin debug bar sits in that strip and takes no room. The fal copy panel now follows a copy already running to its end.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08: get rid of the extra space around the debug button, the profile menu as far right as possible. The spot is pinned in the header's right padding. On the Tools panel, 'already running' used to stop asking for progress, so the end never showed; and a server with no record of the run (after a deploy) now says so and suggests Find.

entries.summary: Admins: while Debug Mode is on, the hidden spot beside the account button shows as a small red bar (a click opens the debug panel). It is half as wide.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08. The page asks once after an admin signs in, and the bar follows every change to Debug Mode (with the red recording dot). Never shown to anyone who is not an admin. Turned off, it is invisible in the same room as before.

entries.summary: Pictures that never reached our storage (still on fal) are now copied there: nightly, before the monthly clean-up, and from Dashboard > Tools.
entries.detail: When copying a new picture to our storage fails, the picture keeps fal's address so it is not lost; fal does not keep files for ever. On 21-22 October an R2 key problem left 18 storyboard pictures on staging that way, and a video cut made from them could not be saved. services/falCopy.js finds every fal address in this site's database, copies each file once into this site's own bucket (through the usual upload, so staging to staging's bucket and production to production's), and points every row that used it at the copy, one transaction per picture; the archive's source_url follows, so archived marks stay. A picture fal no longer has is listed and left alone; the rights verdict follows each copy. Logs, the rights record and video_shots.fal_video_url are not touched. Runs once a night after 3 am Eastern (an email only when it did something or something failed), at the start of the monthly clean-up, and from the new panel under the orphan check: Find (only looks) and Copy them to our storage.

entries.summary: Admins: while Debug Mode is on, one click on the hidden spot beside the account button opens My Account with the debug panel open.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-08. While Debug Mode is off, seven clicks still turn it on; while it is on, turn it off from the panel.

entries.summary: Video tab: when a cut cannot be saved, the reason is shown beside the button and written to the debug log.
entries.detail: TD-090. On staging every save of a cut (its name, the model's own sound) and Write the shot list failed with no reason shown. Each refusal and failure of a cut's save and of the shot list now goes to the server log and, with Debug Mode on, to the debug log: the reason, what was sent, and any picture whose address is not a Campaignia one. A save reply that is not JSON (a gateway page) is named as such. The shot list job logs each step: pictures read, each call to the writer, the reply's first words when it fails the checks, the fill and the charge. Nothing else changes.

entries.summary: Video tab: pick a style for each cut (Animated, Living Illustration, Documentary) and let Campaignia write the shot list.
entries.detail: TD-090, Video Phase 2 build 3. Write the shot list sends the version's story, the cut's pictures (small, as pictures and as words), the cast, the art style, the genre, the style's rules and the video model's lengths to the model that writes the story, and fills the overall direction and every shot box (action, camera, lines for Animated, sound, length). It runs as a job; the boxes wait while it is written; Rewrite asks first. Costs one token, or one per 8 cents of the real model cost when more, charged only when the boxes are filled; a refused or interrupted list costs nothing. The book's narrative is never changed. The clips themselves stay free.

entries.summary: Video tab: every field of a draft cut saves the moment you leave it, as well as while you type.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: make sure the fields save on blur. Name, video model, sound, overall direction, each shot box and each shot length now save at once when they lose focus (vlFlushSave), instead of only after the short pause while typing.

entries.summary: Picking another version while the Video tab is open now shows that version's cuts.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: switching versions did not load the cuts on the Video tab. onForkChange now reopens the tab when it is the one showing, and a draft typed a moment before is saved first.

entries.summary: The Video Lab is now the Video tab: cuts made from the storyboard, laid out like the Storyboard, one pinned per version.
entries.detail: TD-090, Video Phase 2 build 2. New cut takes the version on screen and its storyboard pictures, title picture first (the Canonical one when the version has none). The open cut looks like the Storyboard: picture cards with a shot card between each pair, the overall direction above, theme colours only so it follows the brand. Move, Replace and Remove pictures, add any from the Archive, name it; a draft saves itself as you type. Generate makes the shots and joins them as the Lab did; a made cut plays full width with its shots underneath (Redo, Download), and Copy to a new cut starts a new draft from it. The star pins one cut per version. The Lab runs made on a session become cuts of its Canonical. Behind the video switch, admins always.

entries.summary: Dashboard: a Video switch beside The Guild and Brands, all three on one row. Admins always have the Video Lab; the switch gives it to everyone else.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: make it always work for admins, the on and off for everyone else. app_settings.video_lab_on, read on every Video Lab call, so switching off stops the next request. With it on, a member sees and makes videos only in their own campaigns and only from that campaign Archive; renaming, redoing, joining again and deleting are for the member who made the video or the Story Master. No tokens are charged for video yet, and the switch says so.

entries.summary: The move arrows, x and gripper on the Storyboard, Review and session cards are 30% smaller.
entries.detail: Ian: shrink them by 30%. Text 11px to 8px, height 18px to 13px (session cards 24px to 17px), gripper 16px to 11px, gaps 4px to 3px. Nothing else changes.

entries.summary: Story Masters can now put sessions in any order: arrows and a drag handle on each session card.
entries.detail: TD-933 build 2. Bottom right of each session card, beside the Draft or Ready chip and the menu: a left arrow, a right arrow and a drag handle, for the Story Master only. The arrows follow the page, which shows the newest session first: left moves a card toward the front (later in the story), right moves it toward the back (earlier in the story). The drag handle drops a card anywhere. Publish, the book and the session arrows on the Storyboard follow the new order. The order is saved whole and refused if the list changed in the meantime, in which case the page reloads it.

entries.summary: Sessions now keep a place in their campaign list; every list and book reads it. Nothing looks different yet.
entries.detail: TD-933 build 1. Ian: ordering sessions by date is a little hit and miss, so each session now has a place (sessions.sort_order, 1, 2, 3 within a campaign). The first start numbers every campaign exactly as its list read before: date, then the order made, then id. The Sessions page, the session arrows, Publish, the printed book, the campaign tile picture, the bookshelf, Import Looks and every earlier-session rule (a character look carried forward, the version style, the previous session summary) read the place first, with the old order behind it. A new session goes to the end of the list. One accepted change: two sessions on the same date now count as one before the other for character looks. The arrows to move a session come in the next build.

entries.summary: Video Lab: any number of pictures in order, a prompt between each, joined into one video.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: N pictures in order with a prompt between each image, like the storyboard, and an overall prompt too. Pictures are added and changed in the Archive window, moved up or down and taken out; between each pair is what happens and how long that clip runs; the overall prompt goes into every clip. Generate sends every clip to fal at once; when the last is saved, fal joins them (fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/merge-videos) and the joined video is stored. Redo remakes one clip and joins again; Join again retries a failed join. Past runs are short rows; a click opens one to the full player with each clip underneath. Runs from v3.4.86 to v3.4.89 show as two-picture videos.

entries.summary: Video Lab: a spinner while a video is being made, and a much bigger player.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: a progress spinner, and the video viewer much bigger. A run still being made shows a large spinner with how long it has been going (refreshed every 10 seconds) and a note that it usually takes a few minutes; Generate shows a small spinner while sending. A finished video plays as wide as the panel allows (up to 1100px, and no taller than most of the screen), with the start and end pictures underneath.

entries.summary: Video Lab: click the start or end picture to choose it in the Archive window.
entries.detail: TD-090. Ian: click the start or end picture to open the Archive window, and no Archive grid on the page. Each picture box now opens the same Archive window Replace uses (filters, Clear filters, the pin), titled for the start or the end picture; choosing a picture puts it in that box. Change and Clear sit under a chosen picture. The grid and filter bar below the form are gone.

entries.summary: Video Lab tab (admin only) after Preview on each session.
entries.detail: TD-090. Pick a start and an end picture from the campaign Archive (same filters as the Archive screen), type what happens between them, choose the model and the duration (the choices follow the model), give it a name (defaults to Video Lab and the date and time), and Generate. The cost fal is expected to charge shows before sending. Runs list below, newest first: player, Download, rename, Delete (asks first), status, time taken, the two pictures and the prompt; the list refreshes every 10 seconds while anything is being made. Hidden from everyone but admins.

entries.summary: Video Lab (admin only), server side: make a test video from two Archive pictures with fal.
entries.detail: TD-090, spec claude/VIDEO_SPEC.md. New routes/videoLab.js at /api/video-lab, admin only: model list (Seedance 2.0 and 2.0 Fast, Kling 3.0 Standard, Veo 3.1 Fast, all on fal), make a run, rename, delete (clip removed from storage), download a clip as a file. Runs are rows in two new tables, video_projects and video_shots (shaped for many shots per video later), so they survive a closed browser or a deploy. fal reports back on its webhook; a sweep every 30 seconds catches any it missed. Clips are copied to R2 under video-lab. No tokens are charged; the expected fal cost is recorded. The tab comes in v3.4.87.

entries.summary: Admins choose on the Dashboard which brands are on; with more than one on, people pick theirs on My Account.
entries.detail: TD-1105. New Dashboard section Brands on this site, beside The Guild switch: a tick box per brand (Campaignia, Story), saved as app_settings.brands_enabled. Two or more on: the Brand Theme choice appears on My Account and each person picks, and an account on Story gets its look, words, emails and help wording. One on: the choice goes away and everyone sees that brand. Accounts keep their own pick underneath. At least one stays on. Not set: production Campaignia only, staging every brand, as before. The staging ?brand= switch still shows any brand. Replaces the live flag as the rule.

entries.summary: The last three browser pop-up boxes are now the app's own windows.
entries.detail: Ian, 2026-11-07: no browser boxes anywhere. Copying an invite link on a browser that cannot write to the clipboard now opens our own window with the link and a Copy button (was the browser prompt). Admin only: Dashboard Testers Turn off, and the double-click Reset AI image grows on the Optimize tab, now ask in our own window (were browser confirm boxes). Nothing else changed.

entries.summary: Story emails show the Campaignia logo beside the Campaignia heading.
entries.detail: Ian: the logo can still go on Story emails. The heading that replaces the dark banner picture now has the chest logo beside the word Campaignia, as in the app header, using the small picture the emails already send (Campaignia_Favicon.png). Campaignia emails unchanged.

entries.summary: Story: emails to Story accounts use Story's colors, with Campaignia as a text heading instead of the banner picture.
entries.detail: Ian chose option B: on Story the dark Campaignia banner picture would sit as a dark block on a light email. For an account whose home brand is Story, each email color (the eleven theme names emails use) is swapped for Story's value from its theme sheet, and the banner picture becomes the word Campaignia as text in Story's heading color and font. The product is still Campaignia; the logo stays for now. Campaignia accounts and production are unchanged.

entries.summary: Help: the getting-started steps no longer say moments cannot be moved.
entries.detail: Brain section 1a step 9 still said moments cannot be moved or removed, from before free order (v3.4.32 to v3.4.44); the help chat repeated it to Ian. It now says they can be moved with the arrows or the gripper, and points to Move panels and bridges anywhere; a picture panel still cannot be removed.

entries.summary: Getting started guide reads properly on Story; step 1 reworded.
entries.detail: Ian on Story: step 1 said Create a story / Your campaign holds the whole story, and step 4 Create a chapter/chapter. The guide's step text was wrongly on the page swap's keep list; it now swaps too. A swap that doubles one of the brand's words (chapter/chapter, story story) folds back to one word, on screen and in emails. Step 1 (and Brain section 1a) now say Your campaign holds all of its sessions, which reads as Your story holds all of its chapters on Story.

entries.summary: Story: emails and the help assistant say story and chapter too.
entries.detail: Ian: swap campaign for story and session for chapter in the emails and the Brain; the product stays Campaignia and the logo stays. Emails to an account whose home brand is Story get the words swapped in the subject and the email's own wording (never inside links, tags or styles), while names people typed (campaign and character names, book titles, gift messages) are kept as written; reports to support and Guild messages are sent unchanged. The help assistant is told the person's brand words on each question (from the brand on screen). Production does nothing while only Campaignia is live.

entries.summary: A member opening Publish on the Story Master's version no longer sees "Something went wrong".
entries.detail: Ian, with a newly invited member viewing the Canonical on Prep & Preview. The first-open snapshot save (title, title color, cover) ran because the page counts a member with no version of their own as owning the Canonical (TD-254, still open), while the server refuses it; the refusal popped up. The background save now runs only where the server agrees: your own version, the Canonical for its Story Master, or a curating Story Master. A change the member makes themselves still gets the switch-to-your-own-version message. Also: the Publish subtitle now reads Your complete campaign (Your complete story on Story, where the word swap had made it story story).

entries.summary: Story: campaigns are called stories and sessions chapters.
entries.detail: Ian chose option A for now: a small script, public/js/brand-words.js, swaps whole words on screen for brands with a word list (Story: campaign to story, session to chapter, keeping plural and case). It never touches form fields or the places that show people's own words (names, descriptions, panel titles, narrative, captions), and it stops at once on Campaignia. Option B, each place asking the brand for its word, comes later with the full word list.

entries.summary: Story: faint labels across the app (panel style lines, Moment and Bridge headers and the like) are darker.
entries.detail: Ian on staging, Story brand: the style line under a panel title (Watercolor, Discovery, Fullpage) and the 6 - MOMENT header were too faint. Every text color written as see-through accent in the app (89 in style.css, 26 in app.html, 28 in app.js) now uses --accent-text-rgb from v3.4.74: the same gold on Campaignia, dark periwinkle on Story, so the faint labels keep their lightness but read. Also from Ian: the Edit prompt / Regen / Retouch / Replace / Lock / Archive buttons over a picture had turned light in v3.4.73 and were hard to read on the dark frame; they are back to dark glass with accent text on every brand.

entries.summary: Account page: a Brand Theme choice, so anyone can switch between Campaignia and Story.
entries.detail: Ian: everyone may switch, and customers switch themselves. A Brand Theme dropdown on the Account page lists the brands this person may pick and saves the pick to users.home_brand (GET and PUT /api/auth/brand, own account only). The save also updates the brand cached in the session, so the page reloads in the new brand at once. The section only shows when there is more than one brand to pick, so it stays hidden on production while only Campaignia is live. When a staging switch or the BRAND variable outranks the account, the page says so.

entries.summary: Story: faint labels in the library, the Guild and the Retouch panel are readable.
entries.detail: Ian on staging, Story brand. Small text in the accent color (library header link, Gallery/Books/The Guild tabs, filter and Guild role buttons, footers, form placeholders) now uses a new theme name, --accent-text: the same gold on Campaignia, dark periwinkle on Story. Story's --gold-dim (Retouch panel subtitle, Marker size, the Optional: click lines, many app hints) and --warn-text are now dark too. The impersonation banner's Add tokens button and the small x over marketplace pictures go back to dark glass, since they sit on orange or on a picture.

entries.summary: Story: buttons, chips and the account menu on a light page are light, not grey or brown.
entries.detail: Ian on staging: the grey buttons on Review (Edit Image Prompt, Add character and the like) could not be read on Story. They, and every other plain see-through black background in the app (56 of them; the Details button on the dark books keeps its dark glass), now use the theme's --glass-rgb: black on Campaignia, so nothing changes there; white on Story. Shadows and the dark gradients over pictures stay as they were. Also from Ian: the account menu was dark brown with dark text on Story. The solid dark surfaces (app header, account menu, corner menu, selected chips, novel cover and chapter headers) now use a new theme name, --ink-bg: the same dark brown on Campaignia, pale lavender on Story. And the description and fork lines on the dark campaign and session books use a new --on-book-rgb, parchment on every brand, since the books stay dark.

entries.summary: Story: a stand-in light palette for the inside of the app (proof of concept).
entries.detail: brand2.css gets light values for 104 more theme names, worked out from the Sky and Lavender palette by how each name is used, so the app is readable as Story for the marketing demo (Ian: "this is to prove the concept"). Rough by design; the designer's palette replaces it. Also: the app's darkening of the background picture, the dark halo behind page titles and the page title gold now follow the theme (--picture-dim and the new --page-title), so Story's app is not greyed over; Campaignia's values are unchanged. Story is not live on production.

entries.summary: Two brands: the background picture is a theme setting (Story gets its watercolor wash); brand 2 is named Story.
entries.detail: The tavern picture behind the app, the campaigns screen, sign-in, invite, gift, redeem, 404 and the Library is now the theme's --page-picture: Campaignia's sheet holds the same picture, so Campaignia looks the same; brand 2's holds its watercolor wash in place of a picture. Brand 2's name in the brand list is Story (Ian; the internal key stays brand2). Also the hover on Amended appearance (session Characters tab) now says Save keeps it (was Approve change).

entries.summary: Help assistant: the Characters tab answers match the redesigned Edit window.
entries.detail: Brain section 10.2 and the troubleshooting answer for a character whose look changes: the red Change Detected band (was a review badge), Save keeps a retouch (was Approve change), Revert and Cancel, Ignore suggested change, and the Change Starts at Moment dropdown (was Change first appears at this Moment Panel). Text only.

entries.summary: Two brands groundwork: each page is given its brand; accounts remember theirs; a staging switch.
entries.detail: New services/brands.js: the brand list (Campaignia, live; brand 2, not live yet) and the rule that picks each page's brand: the staging switch (?brand=brand2 on any page, remembered by that browser; ?brand=clear), the BRAND Railway variable (staging only), a brand's own web address (none yet), the signed-in person's brand, the landing page they came through (/story is brand 2's), else Campaignia. A brand that is not live is never chosen on production. New column users.home_brand (text, every existing account 'campaignia'); a new account takes the brand it signed up through. Every page (app, sign-in, gift, redeem, invite, reset, landing pages, Library, legal pages, 404, offline) reads the brand and lays brand 2's theme over Campaignia's when it applies; /story's own address check from v3.4.68 is replaced by this. On production nothing changes while brand 2 is not live.

entries.summary: /story picks its look by web address: brand 2 on chroniclemygame.com (staging), Campaignia's on campaignia.com.
entries.detail: So the brand work can be promoted without showing the new look in production (Ian, 2026-11-06). /story links Campaignia's theme sheet; on chroniclemygame.com (staging) it also writes in brand 2's sheet, which overrides every name, and sets the light toolbar color. On campaignia.com and any other address /story looks as it did before v3.4.63. brand2.css and the brand 2 font files ship but are used only on chroniclemygame.com. Temporary: the server-side brand switch replaces this.

entries.summary: Brand 2 on /story: Storybook fonts (Fraunces, Lora, Quicksand, Patrick Hand).
entries.detail: The landing page fonts are now theme names: --font-heading, --font-body, --font-label and --font-comic (landing.css, landing-story.css and the tier grid use them). Campaignia's sheet holds today's fonts, so the home page and /game-masters look the same (one small difference: eleven rules that said 'Crimson Text', serif now also list Georgia before serif, which only matters if the font fails to load). Brand 2's sheet holds Ian's pick, Storybook: Fraunces headings, Lora body, Quicksand labels, Patrick Hand for the comic bits. The 13 font files are plain files in public/fonts/brand2 with their Open Font License text; the print font list is not touched.

entries.summary: /story: the space above and below the hero picture matches the panel beside it.
entries.detail: Ian on staging: the strip above and below the turning-page picture was the page color, lighter than the text panel next to it. The picture slot, the page under it and the page-turn sweep now use --panel-deep, the left panel's color. landing-story.css is used by /story only.

entries.summary: Compare the Tiers is readable on brand 2's light page.
entries.detail: Ian on staging /story: the middle of Compare the Tiers was unreadable (dark panel behind dark text). The grid's panel color pointed at a text-color name (--surface-ink-text), which brand 2 sets dark. It now points at the background name --panel. On Campaignia's pages the grid panel moves from #160e06 to #140c04, the same fold Ian approved in v3.4.58; it cannot be seen.

entries.summary: Brand 2 on /story: the halftone dots are barely there and the text is easier to read.
entries.detail: Ian on staging: the dots were too dark and some text was hard to read. The halftone dot color is now a theme name, --halftone-dot (Campaignia keeps its rgba(0,0,0,0.15), so the Campaignia landing pages are unchanged); brand 2's is a faint slate blue at 4.5 percent. Brand 2's two text colors are deeper: on-panel #3f4668 to #262b4a, accent-pale #6a74a6 to #4f5a94.

entries.summary: Two brands: /story gets brand 2's own light look, Sky and Lavender.
entries.detail: New theme sheet css/themes/brand2.css: the same names as campaignia.css, with the storyteller brand's values chosen by Ian from the pastel trial (cool paper, slate-blue ink, periwinkle accent, pink button, a soft watercolor wash behind the page). /story now links that sheet instead of Campaignia's, and its browser toolbar color is the light page color. Every other page is unchanged. Fonts and layout are the same for now; fonts are next.

entries.summary: Two brands: the tier badges take their colors from the theme sheet, and names nothing used are gone from it.
entries.detail: The Copper, Silver, Gold and Platinum badges and headers in the app (Account, Plans and Passes) now read their colors from css/themes/campaignia.css: seven new tier names, exact colors; Gold uses the brand gold. The theme sheet loses 20 names nothing in the code base uses any more: the folded names that only pointed at their replacements (gold, gold-light, parchment, cream, crimson, surface-ink, window-bg and the rest), two old light tokens, and two hex forms whose rgb forms are the ones in use. Nothing on screen changes.

entries.summary: Two brands, round 3: the public pages now take their colors from the theme sheet.
entries.detail: The home page, /game-masters, /story, the tier grid, the public library, the four legal pages, the 404 page, the offline page, the install chip and the marketplace screens now name their colors from css/themes/campaignia.css, and each page links that sheet. Their own local color names (ink, gold, parchment and so on, which clashed with the theme's) are replaced by the theme's names. The tier grid keeps its --tg- names but points them at the brand, so it matches the landing page it sits on. The sheet gains names for the tier metals (silver, platinum), the AI tag, the writer and editor labels and the added-to-shelf button. Near-identical shades are folded in as agreed on the review sheet; the offline page carries each color as a fallback too. Left typed: black and white shadows, near-black, and the staging header.

entries.summary: Two brands: email colors come from the theme sheet.
entries.detail: email.js no longer types its 203 colors; the server reads them from public/css/themes/campaignia.css (new services/themeColors.js) and writes the color into each email, since email programs ignore CSS var(). The email button keeps its red as --button-cta. The dark area around each email is a touch darker (it now uses the panel color).

entries.summary: Two brands: the sign-in, gift, redeem, invite and reset-password pages take their colors from the theme sheet.
entries.detail: 136 colors on login, gift, redeem, invite and reset-password now use 22 existing theme names (no new names; two solid/see-through forms added). Near-identical shades take the name's color, so a few shift very slightly. The reset page's old --gold now uses --accent-bright. Black, white and greys stay as typed.

entries.summary: Two brands: theme names that held the same or nearly the same color were combined (14 names folded into 6).
entries.detail: Folded: gold into accent-bright, gold-light into accent-pale, parchment into on-panel, on-panel-cream into on-panel, cream into on-panel, crimson into danger, error-fill into danger, surface-ink into panel, panel-alt into panel, modal into panel, panel-raised into panel, window-bg into panel, card into panel, panel-deeper into panel-deep. style.css, app.html and app.js now use the kept names; each folded name stays in the theme sheet pointing at its replacement until the other pages are swept. The light text on dark panels is now one cream and the delete red one red, so a few colors shift very slightly.

entries.summary: Two brands, step 3: every remaining color is named by its job in the theme sheet, and near-identical shades were merged (a few colors shift very slightly).
entries.detail: About 600 colors still typed into style.css, app.html and app.js (roughly 300 different shades) now use about 90 names in css/themes/campaignia.css, each named for what it does (labels, highlights, warnings, errors, success, the shelf's wood and brass...). Near-identical shades were merged into one as Ian approved on 2026-11-06, so some colors shift slightly. Kept as typed: black and white shadows, the staging header, the tier colors, the admin AI-layout window and the title halo. The error dialog keeps its exact grey under its own name.

entries.summary: Two brands, step 2b: the colors app.js writes into the page now come from the theme sheet (nothing looks different).
entries.detail: Every brand color app.js writes as CSS (style attributes in built HTML, cssText, element.style) now names a value from css/themes/campaignia.css. Proved identical: expanded back it is the old file. Left as typed: the tier colors (tier identity, not brand), the SVG chart grid lines, the admin AI-layout JSON window (a window of its own, without the theme sheet) and the on-picture title halo. Also puts back the error dialog's own background (#1c1b22), which v3.4.54 had turned brown by defining --panel.

entries.summary: Two brands, step 2a: app.html's colors now come from the theme sheet (nothing looks different).
entries.detail: Every brand color typed into app.html's style attributes and style blocks now names a value from css/themes/campaignia.css, which gains four names for the bookshelf look (foil, tooling, shelf shadow, inset well). Proved identical: expanded back it is the old file, and every computed style matches. Left as typed: the meta theme-color (the browser reads it before any style sheet) and comments.

entries.summary: Two brands, step 1: Campaignia's colors now come from a theme sheet (nothing looks different).
entries.detail: style.css names every brand color (gold accent, dark panels, parchment text, crimson) and reads its value from css/themes/campaignia.css, so a second brand can have its own sheet. Proved identical: expanded back it is the old file, and every computed style of every element on the tested screens matches.

entries.summary: Clearer wording for when a character change starts.
entries.detail: In a character's Edit window, Change Starts at Moment explains on hover that the character keeps their earlier look until that moment, then the change takes effect and carries into the next session; Empty applies it to the whole session.

entries.summary: Dashboard Stats user list: columns reordered and renamed, and a Refresh button.
entries.detail: Days, Name, Email, Last Action DT, Last Action, Tier, Pass, Expires, Status, then any other column the view has. Refresh reloads the list.

entries.summary: A change Generate Story spotted now shows as a red band across the character's picture.
entries.detail: On a session's Characters tab, Change Detected - Edit for Details sits across the bottom of the picture in larger type, and a new picture waiting to be saved shows the same way in gold. Click either to open Edit.

entries.summary: An approved character change no longer reappears in the Edit window, and a suggested change says what to do.
entries.detail: Once a change is approved, the Amended appearance box opens empty for the next one; the change stays in the Description, which is what the pictures are drawn from. A change Generate Story suggests now explains itself: retouch to apply it, or ignore it. A second change adds to the first instead of replacing it.

entries.summary: The character Edit window has one Save, Revert, and Regenerate in Art Style.
entries.detail: Beside Retouch image are Regenerate in Art Style and, when the AI suggested a change, Ignore suggested change. Retouch and Regenerate now build on each other. Replace and Archive stay on the picture after a retouch, and Revert goes back to the saved picture. One Save keeps everything as it is in the window. The description pop-up on the cards opens above the line and no longer flickers.

entries.summary: A session's Characters tab shows picture cards, and Edit opens a window.
entries.detail: The characters are laid out across the tab as picture cards, like the Characters screen, with one line of the description (hover to read it all). Edit opens a window with the picture beside the boxes, so a retouch appears next to what you typed. A retouch keeps going if you close the window: the card shows it working and then New image ready. During Regenerate in Art Style every card waiting its turn shows that it is waiting. Approve change now saves an edited description too.

entries.summary: Bigger character pictures on a session's Characters tab, with the description beside them.
entries.detail: Each character's picture is larger, and the name and description sit to its right. A long description is cut to fit beside the picture; hover over it to read it all. On a phone the picture sits on top with the whole description below.

entries.summary: Names under the pictures in the picture pickers are larger and easier to read.
entries.detail: In every window where you pick a character, asset or picture, the names under the pictures are bigger, bolder and brighter, and the Characters tab link in the + Add character note is gold instead of blue.

entries.summary: Add A Character on a session's Characters tab brings in someone Generate Story missed.
entries.detail: Pick a campaign character from the pictures and they join the session's cast with their latest look in this version (or the Canonical's, or their own look if neither has one). The Review and Storyboard + Add character windows now list only the session's cast, with a note pointing to Add A Character for anyone else. If Generate Story would take a character out of the cast because their name is not in the Story or the notes, it names them and asks first.

entries.summary: The character-change dropdown numbers its pictures as the Story panels do.
entries.detail: On the Characters tab, “Change first appears at this Moment Panel” now lists each picture with its number and title as the Story panels and the Review show them, so after panels move the numbers match the page.

entries.summary: The Writing Coach checks that each box makes sense after everything before it on the page.
entries.detail: Feedback now reads the whole page up to the box and checks continuity first: a character gaining something they already had, an event repeated or undone, time running backwards with no flashback. It names the row it clashes with, numbered as the page numbers them. Regen writes for the page as it now reads, and handles a moved picture as a flashback or flash-forward on purpose.

entries.summary: Story moves: a new version no longer marks every bridge out of place; a bridge after the title prints as its own paragraph.
entries.detail: Copying a session to a new version keeps its bridges where they were written, so no out-of-place notes appear until something is moved (versions already copied are put right when next opened). A bridge placed right after the title now prints as its own paragraph after the Opening. Rewriting a bridge (typing, Regen, the Coach) removes its out-of-place note straight away.

entries.summary: Small fixes from testing: the Company page, the cover warning, Help, and two warnings for rearranged stories.
entries.detail: Include Sup. Characters / NPCs now hides with the character page. When both your cover picture’s title and subtitle differ from the book’s, both are said at once. Help tries once more by itself before saying it could not answer. Regenerate Narrative asks first on a rearranged story, and Regen says Use this replaces the whole box.

entries.summary: Every row of the story is numbered in order, Opening to Closing.
entries.detail: On the Story panels and the Review tab every row now has a number from the top: 1 – Opening, then each picture and each bridge (shown simply as “3 – Bridge”), and the Closing last. The numbers follow the page, so they change as you move things.

entries.summary: Clean-up: the older panel-move code is gone.
entries.detail: The routes and page code from the first designs of panel moving (v3.4.32-35: pictures-only arrows, swapping bridges, the first drag) are removed. Every move now goes through one route; nothing a user sees changes.

entries.summary: A bridge can now sit right after the title picture; the book prints it after the Opening.
entries.detail: Moving a bridge (or deleting the first panel) can put a bridge straight after the title picture. It shows there on the Story panels and the Review tab, and the printed book places it right after the Opening. Books nobody has rearranged print exactly as before.

entries.summary: Move story panels and bridges anywhere, separately.
entries.detail: On your own version, every picture panel and every bridge on the Story panels and the Review tab has arrows that move it one place (trading places with whatever is next to it) and a gripper to drag it anywhere, with a gold line showing where it will land. Bridges are numbered down the page and named after the pictures either side. The x on a bridge deletes it. Locked pictures can be moved. The title picture and Opening stay first.

entries.summary: Story text: every bridge has an id of its own, ready for moving panels and bridges anywhere.
entries.detail: Behind the scenes, the first step of free ordering (TD-1107): each bridge carries its own id and keeps it when panels move, are deleted or the narrative is saved. Deleting a panel now keeps the bridges after it, after the panel before it. A new route arranges a version in any order; the page uses it from v3.4.37.

entries.summary: Story panels move without their bridges; bridges move on their own.
entries.detail: Moving a panel now leaves the bridge text where it is. Each bridge is numbered and named after the panels either side, and has its own arrows and x to swap it with a neighbour or empty it. Drag panels and bridges by the new gripper beside the arrows.

entries.summary: Drag story panels into a new order.
entries.detail: On a computer, drag a panel by its moment bar on the Story panels, or by the top of its row on the Review tab, and drop it on another panel. The arrows still work, including on phones.

entries.summary: Move and delete story panels.
entries.detail: On your own version, each panel has arrows and an x on the Story panels and the Review tab. A panel's picture, text, directions and outline move with it. Locked panels and the title picture stay where they are. Deleting a panel cannot be undone.

entries.summary: Groundwork for moving and deleting story panels: each panel's text is now linked to it.
entries.detail: A panel and its text, Directions, outline and character-change marker move together in one step. The buttons come in the next update.

entries.summary: Prep & Preview and the Image Builder open one panel at a time.
entries.detail: Opening a panel closes the one that was open, so the list stays short. The panel you used last is open when you come back.

entries.summary: Books: a character page picture keeps its heading just above it and its text just below.
entries.detail: On a character page that uses an Archive picture, the heading, the picture and the text below are centred on the page together, so a wide picture no longer leaves the heading alone at the top.

entries.summary: The Company Page panel is more compact, and the tour knows the new panels.
entries.detail: The Heading and Text below boxes sit beside the Company picture, which is greyed out while the character page is the line-up. The Publish tour walks through the new panels.

entries.summary: Prep & Preview: the settings are in the order of the book.
entries.detail: The panels now run Cover, Title Page, Author's Note Page, The Company Page, Table of Contents, Body and Back Cover, each with the settings for that part of the book. Apply & preview is gone: changes save as you make them and Refresh preview shows them.

entries.summary: Books: name your character page and add words under it.
entries.detail: Layout has a Heading box for the character page (it starts as The Company; call it The Cast, or leave it empty) and a Text below box. On the line-up the text starts as the names from left to right and stays up to date until you change it. A Company picture now gets the same frame as your other pictures.

entries.summary: Books: use a picture from your Archive as the character page instead of the line-up.
entries.detail: Prep & Preview has a Company tile beside Cover, Back and Title. Pick a picture there, such as one made in the Image Builder, and the character page shows it, fitted to the page. Layout now lists Include cover page and Include table of contents first.

entries.summary: Prep & Preview: Refresh preview flashes bright and wiggles every time you change something.
entries.detail: The button lights up gold for a moment with each change, then keeps a soft glow until you refresh, so it is easy to see that the preview is out of date.

entries.summary: Prep & Preview: the title settings sit in their own panel under the cover pictures, hidden when your cover picture has its title.
entries.detail: Tick My Cover Picture has Title Included to hide the title style, placement, size and Title Builder. For an Image Builder cover, a line says if the title on the picture differs from your book's title.

entries.summary: Book covers: tick "Cover picture has the title" to show a titled picture without a second title over it.
entries.detail: In Prep & Preview, the new tick box under the title and subtitle leaves the front cover to your picture alone, such as an Image Builder picture archived with its title. The spine and the title page still carry the title.

entries.summary: Image Builder: pick several scenes or assets at once, search assets by name, and pin the scene filters.
entries.detail: In + Add scene and + Add asset, click pictures to tick them, then press Add to bring them all in. The asset window has a search box for the name, and the scene window's Pin keeps your filters for next time.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Move Title and Move Writing on the picture, to move or resize what is laid on it.
entries.detail: Press Move Title (or Move Writing on a handout) to select it where it sits, drag it or resize it from its corner, then Apply, for free. Remove title and Remove writing now show only while it is selected, and Delete sits beside Mark Ready.

entries.summary: Choosing a character's look: each card shows its session, date and art style, with the versions behind a …
entries.detail: The list of versions that use a picture now opens from a small … pill on the card, so every card stays short and easy to compare.

entries.summary: Image Builder: the Scenes picker has the Archive's filters and loads as you scroll.
entries.detail: Narrow the scenes by session, version, moment name, character, who archived it, art style and shape, newest or oldest first. Pictures load as you scroll down, so a big Archive opens quickly.

entries.summary: Image Builder: add scenes from the campaign's Archive as references, as vignettes on a poster and more.
entries.detail: A new Scenes row in References brings in archived story panels and Image Builder pictures. A poster fits them in as smaller vignettes; a portrait puts them in the background; a handout prints them on the document; an item showcase adds a small inset; a character study swaps one close-up for the scene; an action scene uses them to guide what the characters do. Each is redrawn in the picture's art style.

entries.summary: Campaign pins appear once you have five or more campaigns.
entries.detail: With four or fewer there is little to sort, so the pins stay out of the way; any pins you set are kept and still decide the order.

entries.summary: The Image Builder's and Import a character's campaign pickers now follow your My Campaigns order.
entries.detail: Pinned campaigns come first, marked with the pin, then the ones you opened most recently. Choosing a campaign in the Image Builder counts as opening it.

entries.summary: My Campaigns: the pin sits on the card without a circle behind it.
entries.detail: A little larger, with a soft shadow so it shows on light covers.

entries.summary: My Campaigns: pin campaigns to the top, and the rest are listed by when you last opened them.
entries.detail: Each campaign has a pin in its corner. Pinned campaigns stay at the top in the order you pinned them; the others follow, the one you opened most recently first. Your pins and order are your own and follow you to any device.

entries.summary: Image Builder: on a phone the picture's buttons sit under it, and opening a picture from the Gallery closes the form's panels.
entries.detail: Regen, Retouch, Edit Prompt and the rest now sit in a row under the picture on a phone, as on the Storyboard. A picture opened from the Gallery shows with every panel of the form shut, so the picture and its buttons are in view; New picture opens them again.

entries.summary: Map to Scene is shown to admins only while it is tested.
entries.detail: It is out of the Image type list and the help assistant for everyone else; pictures already made with it keep working.

entries.summary: Click a character or asset pill to see its picture, in the Image Builder and on the Storyboard.
entries.detail: In the Image Builder's References, a character pill shows the look you picked and an asset pill its picture. On the Storyboard and Review, character pills now open the character's picture for that session, as asset pills already did. The x on a pill still only removes it.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Map to Scene takes a map saved as an Item, and turns dungeon and cave maps into a cutaway of the real place.
entries.detail: The map can be an Item asset (or a Location). It is used only as the plan of the place, so the picture shows the place itself rather than a map. Outdoor maps are seen from a low hilltop; dungeons, caves and buildings as a cutaway from above with the ceiling lifted off.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Map to Scene turns a flat map into a painted view of the real place.
entries.detail: Add the map to the campaign as a Location asset, add it to References, and choose the Map to Scene image type. The picture shows the place from a low hilltop at an angle, keeping the map's layout, with the paper, labels and grid gone.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Make a Copy of your own picture, beside New picture.
entries.detail: A free copy of the picture you have open, as a new Draft with the same words, references, style and title, so you can change and redraw it without touching the original.

entries.summary: Image Builder: the image type's instructions open from an Edit Prompt pill, and the Apply buttons follow the title or writing you are placing.
entries.detail: The blue See / edit instructions link under Image type is now an Edit Prompt pill (Hide Prompt when open). When you place a title or a handout's writing on a picture, Apply and Cancel sit right under the box and move with it, above it when it is near the bottom.

entries.summary: Image Builder: characters and assets you add or remove on one of your pictures are saved to it at once, so Retouch and Regen use them.
entries.detail: With one of your own pictures open, the References list now works like a Story panel's cast: each change is saved to the picture straight away. A character added after the picture was drawn now appears in Retouch, and their reference picture goes with the retouch. A character you remove no longer has their reference sent.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Archive can keep both copies of a titled picture, and Save as Asset always saves the picture without its lettering.
entries.detail: When a picture has a title or text laid on it, Archive now offers Both, which puts the copy with the words and the clean copy in the campaign's Archive together. Save as Asset no longer asks: an asset is always the clean picture.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Retouch names the picture's own art style, and choosing a character's look shows each picture once, side by side.
entries.detail: In the Retouch window, Fix or reapply the art style now names the style of the picture you are retouching (it always used that style; only the label said otherwise). When you choose a character's look, in the Image Builder or in Import a character, a picture shared by several versions appears once with those versions listed under it, and the looks sit side by side instead of one to a row. Each look also shows its art style when it was made with Regenerate in Art Style.

entries.summary: Image Builder: character counters, a better first writing box, and a tidier tour.
entries.detail: The Description and Handout text boxes now show how many of their 1,500 characters you have used. Place writing starts with a smaller box in the middle of the blank area. Create a campaign opens right over the Image Builder. The Image Builder tour counts only the steps you can see, and the note after Apply writing names the button as it reads.

entries.summary: The top bar fits on tablet-sized screens.
entries.detail: Between phone and desktop widths, the top bar no longer pushed the page sideways; it uses the shorter forms of its buttons instead.

entries.summary: Choosing a campaign shows each campaign picture.
entries.detail: When you choose a campaign in the Image Builder, or choose where to import a character from, each campaign now shows its picture, the same one as on My Campaigns.

entries.summary: Compare the Tiers now lists the Image Builder.
entries.detail: The Compare the Tiers grid has a new Image Builder row, under the Writing Coach: it is part of Platinum, and members of a campaign whose Story Master is on Platinum can use it there too.

entries.summary: Image Builder: handout writing is placed by you, Revert keeps the title, and smaller fixes.
entries.detail: A new handout now arrives with a clear writing area and no words on it: drag your writing onto the picture, size it, and press Apply writing here. Revert now brings back the title and the writing exactly as they were with the earlier picture. Also: the Title Builder Generate button shows its token cost, the Title Builder talks about your picture rather than a book when opened from the Image Builder, Generate names every missing field at once, the token count updates as soon as a picture arrives, and the Image Builder offers a Create a campaign button when you have none.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Remove title only shows on your own pictures.
entries.detail: When you open a picture made by another member in the Image Builder, the Title panel no longer offers Remove title, since you cannot change their picture. Make My Copy gives you your own copy to change.

entries.summary: Image Builder: a guided tour, and the help assistant now knows it.
entries.detail: The first time you open the Image Builder, a short tour walks through each part of the page. The help assistant (the ?s button) can now answer questions about the Image Builder: who can use it, picture types, titles, handouts, the Gallery and Make My Copy, and it knows when you are asking from that page.

entries.summary: The ?s help tooltip shows its words again, and a promo code is checked as soon as you leave its box.
entries.detail: The tooltip on the ?s help buttons was opening underneath the bar below the header, so it looked empty; it now opens on top. When signing up, a promo code that has expired, been used up or is for a different plan is now flagged as soon as you leave the promo code box, instead of after you have filled in the whole form.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Item Showcase as a still life, Portrait / Headshot, and Image type moved up.
entries.detail: Item Showcase now paints your items as a still life on a fitting surface, with a soft setting behind and one clear light, whether there is one item or several. Portrait Token is now called Portrait / Headshot. The Image type panel now sits just under References.

entries.summary: Saving no longer fails on a brief file-storage hiccup.
entries.detail: When the file store is briefly unavailable, saving now tries again by itself a few times. If it still cannot save, the message says so in plain words and has a Try again link, and your optimized book stays on screen.

entries.summary: Image Builder: one Remove title button, and Archive names the title and the text.
entries.detail: Remove title takes the title off the picture and out of the Title section; the drawing stays in the Title Builder, so Done & Use brings it back. When a picture has a title or handout text laid on it, Archive and Save as Asset ask With or Without the title, the text, or the title and text, and the Without button on the picture says the same.

entries.summary: Image Builder: placing the title keeps the handout writing in view, and the other way round.
entries.detail: While you place a title, any handout writing already on the picture stays in view, and while you place the writing, the title stays in view, so you can arrange the two together.

entries.summary: Image Builder: a missing field now shakes, and titles come from the Title Builder.
entries.detail: Pressing Title Builder with no title typed, or Generate with something missing, now outlines and shakes the field that needs filling and says what it is. A title typed without Title Builder lettering is no longer drawn into the picture. The words for a handout now sit under the Image type choice, and Remove writing from picture and Remove title from picture take them off again (free; Revert puts them back).

entries.summary: Image Builder: handouts with your exact words, and one Character / Creature Study.
entries.detail: An In-world Handout now has a Handout text section: type the words, choose a font, ink and layout, and they are set on the paper exactly as typed, so the spelling is always right. Drag the box onto the picture to place and size it. Character Study and Creature Study are now one type, Character / Creature Study.

entries.summary: Image Builder: opening a Gallery picture replaces every field with its own.
entries.detail: Opening any picture from the Gallery now fills every field on the left with the picture's own name, description, type, references, title and style, instead of leaving some from the picture before.

entries.summary: Image Builder: no more "generating very quickly" while picking characters and assets.
entries.detail: Opening character lists, looks and assets, and the gallery refreshing, no longer count towards the limit on how fast you can generate, so picking characters quickly no longer stops with that message. Generating still has the same limit.

entries.summary: Image Builder: drag the title onto the picture, drop it and resize it.
entries.detail: The Placement and Size choices are gone. Drag the lettering from the Title section onto the picture, drop it where you want it, drag its corner to resize it, and press Apply title here. Place title on picture does the same without dragging. The spot is kept, so Regen and Retouch put the title back where you placed it.

entries.summary: Image Builder: a dark fade behind laid-on titles, as on covers.
entries.detail: Title lettering laid on an Image Builder picture now gets the same soft dark haze and halo a cover title gets, so it stands out from the picture. Apply title again to give an existing picture the new look.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Apply title in the Title section, and Title Builder Archive, Replace, Retouch and Stash.
entries.detail: Apply title now sits in the Title section, under the lettering, and lays the title on the picture you have open. The Title Builder Archive, Replace from Archive, From Archive, Retouch, Revert and Done & Stash now work for Image Builder titles too, using that campaign Archive.

entries.summary: Image Builder: new Character Study and Movie Poster / Book Cover, and editable type instructions.
entries.detail: Character Study now paints a character sheet: the character head to toe, with three close-ups of their face from different angles. Movie Poster / Book Cover now paints classic key art: a montage of the main characters, the hero up front, a key moment and dramatic lighting. Under the Image type, See / edit instructions shows what the type asks for, and you can change it for one picture; Reset brings the standard text back.
