entries.summary: Image Builder: Title Builder lettering is laid on exactly as designed, and a clean copy is kept.
entries.detail: Lettering made in the Title Builder is now laid over the finished picture exactly as you designed it, at the placement and size you chose, instead of being redrawn by the art style. A clean copy without the title is kept: Archive and Save as Asset ask which version you want, Without title shows it, and Regen and Retouch work on the clean picture and put the title back on. Apply title lays new lettering, or a new placement or size, on a picture already drawn, for free.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Campaign, Assets and Archive buttons beside the campaign.
entries.detail: The campaign line at the top of the Image Builder now has buttons to open the campaign, its Asset Library and its Archive. Back on the Assets and Archive pages returns to the Image Builder.

entries.summary: Image Builder: a Title section, and the name saves when you leave it.
entries.detail: A new Title section, after Description, letters a title and subtitle you type into the picture, at the placement and size you choose. The Title Builder can design the lettering first, from a description and a reference picture; without it the art style decides. A title drawn into a picture cannot be taken out again, so make a version without it if you want the picture for a book cover. Renaming a picture you made now saves as soon as you leave the Name field.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Retouch and Save as Asset, and characters drawn at their set height.
entries.detail: Retouch opens the same Retouch window as story pictures, with its markers and reference picker, and costs one token; Revert brings back the picture from before. Save as Asset makes the picture a campaign asset, and you can frame just part of it. Every character in an Image Builder picture is now described at the height set on the character.

entries.summary: Image Builder: changing campaign starts a blank form, and a description is optional once you choose an image type.
entries.detail: Your pictures stay in the gallery of the campaign they were made in.

entries.summary: Image Builder: the form is in folding panels, with the picture's name on top.
entries.detail: References, Shape, Art style, Image type and Description each have their own panel that opens and closes like the Prep & Preview panels, and remembers how you left it. A closed panel shows your choice in its header. The References panel is easier to read.

entries.summary: Choosing a character's look: versions with no pictures of that character are no longer listed.
entries.detail: Applies to Import a character and the Image Builder's character picker.

entries.summary: Image Builder: the seven picture shapes fit on one row.
entries.detail: On a phone they still wrap onto two rows.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Draft / Ready sits with Generate and New picture, and the form headings match Prep & Preview.
entries.detail: The Draft or Ready label and its Mark Ready / Back to Draft button moved up from under the picture to the row of buttons above it. The form's headings (References, Shape, Art style and the rest) use the same lettering as Prepare to Publish.

entries.summary: Image Builder: a tighter page, Generate and New picture above the picture, and the picture's own buttons on it.
entries.detail: The short description sits beside the title and the page starts closer to the top. Generate and New picture are on the row with the zoom buttons. Edit Prompt, Regen, Revert, Archive and Delete appear on the picture when you point at it, the same way as on story pictures (always shown on a phone).

entries.summary: Image Builder: one scroll bar, and the whole picture always shows.
entries.detail: The picture no longer sits in its own scrolling box. Zooming in makes it bigger up to the width of the page, and the page scrolls as normal.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Edit Prompt, Regen, Revert, Archive and Make My Copy.
entries.detail: Under your picture: Edit Prompt changes the words it is drawn from, Regen draws it again (one token), Revert swaps back to the picture before the last Regen, and Archive puts a copy in the campaign's Archive to use as a cover, title picture or replacement. Opening one of your pictures from the Gallery loads its settings back into the form. On someone else's picture, Make My Copy gives you your own copy to work on, free.

entries.summary: Image Builder: Draft and Ready, a New picture button, and a bigger picture with zoom.
entries.detail: A new picture starts as a Draft that only you can see; Mark Ready shares it with the campaign's gallery, and Back to Draft takes it back. New picture clears the form for the next one (your campaign, shape and art style stay). The picture is shown bigger, with the same zoom buttons as Prep & Preview.

entries.summary: The Image Builder has two tabs: Make a picture and Gallery.
entries.detail: On Make a picture, your picture fills the right side of the page at its own shape, with the same Generating spinner as story pictures while it is drawn. The Gallery shows every picture in the campaign across the whole page; click one to open it.

entries.summary: New: the Image Builder, on the profile menu under Custom Art Styles (Platinum).
entries.detail: Make posters, portraits, maps, handouts and more for a campaign: choose its characters and assets as references, a shape, an art style and an optional image type, describe the picture and press Generate. Each picture costs one token and goes into the campaign's gallery, which every member of the campaign can see. It is open in your own Platinum campaigns and in campaigns whose Story Master is on Platinum.

entries.summary: The Choose an art style window has a Go to Custom Art Styles button at the bottom.
entries.detail: On Platinum it opens your Custom Art Styles page, where New art style starts a new one; on other plans it explains that custom styles are a Platinum feature.

entries.summary: The Author's Note in your book is now printed at the same size as the subtitle.
entries.detail: A very long note on a busy page is set a little smaller so it always fits on the page. Books saved earlier keep the old size until they are optimized again.

entries.summary: Image generation: fal no longer stores our prompts and results, and deletes its copy of each new picture after 30 days.
entries.detail: Every fal call sends X-Fal-Store-IO 0 and a 30-day Object Lifecycle header. Railway FAL_STORE_IO=1 turns storage back on; FAL_CDN_EXPIRY_DAYS changes the days (0 = no header). Our own copy in R2 is unaffected.

entries.summary: Admin: Tiers and Passes has a button at the top that opens the Compare the Tiers grid, as visitors see it.
entries.detail: The same window as the landing page, with the live numbers; it reloads on each press, so it reflects what was just saved.

entries.summary: In the Library, a book's card now opens to its left, so the books to its right stay in view, and the Genre and Art style lists close when the mouse moves away.
entries.detail: To test: hover along a row of spines from left to right and check the next spines stay visible; open Genre, move into the list and tick something, then move away and check it closes after a moment (and stays open if you come straight back).

entries.summary: The Library's tab and filter buttons are easier to read against the background.
entries.detail: Gallery, Books, The Guild, All Time and Show everything have a dark fill when not selected, like the Genre and Art style pickers.

entries.summary: Admin: each Platinum Pass on Tiers and Passes shows what someone who buys it at sign-up gets.
entries.detail: The Free Trial's tokens (a pass sits on top of the trial, so all of them stay) plus the pass's tokens, + (?? Promo Code). Updates as you edit the pass or the Free Trial.

entries.summary: Signing up from a Platinum Pass button now takes you on to buy that pass after you confirm your email.
entries.detail: Before, a pass sign-up landed on the Free Trial with no checkout. To test: from GET THE 3-MONTH PASS (and the 6- and 12-month buttons), sign up, confirm the email, and check the pass checkout opens at the right price; with a Gold-only code, the sign-up stops with the wrong-plan message; with a pass code, the checkout shows the discount.

entries.summary: Signing up for one plan with a promo code meant for another now says so, instead of taking you to full price.
entries.detail: For example a Gold code used from the Silver sign-up button. The message sits by Create Account and the promo box is highlighted; remove the code or go back and choose the plan the code is for. To test: from GET SILVER, sign up with a Gold-only code (stopped, with the message); from GET GOLD, the same code goes through and the Gold checkout shows the discount; a plain sign-up (no plan chosen) with the Gold code is not stopped.

entries.summary: Admin: the tiers' At sign-up line now ends + (?? Promo Code), as a reminder that a code's tokens come on top.
entries.detail: Dashboard, Tiers and Passes.

entries.summary: Admin: each tier on Tiers and Passes shows its monthly tokens and what a new account gets at sign-up.
entries.detail: Free Trial: its monthly tokens plus its sign-up bonus. Copper: what someone joining by invite gets. Silver, Gold and Platinum: what someone who chooses that plan at sign-up gets -- the Free Trial CO and sign-up bonus they keep, plus the plan's monthly tokens and its sign-up bonus. Promo codes not included. The totals update as you type, and changing the Free Trial updates the paid plans.

entries.summary: Bonus tokens from a promo code you entered at sign-up are now given when you make your first purchase.
entries.detail: A once-per-customer code entered at sign-up was counted as already used, so its bonus tokens were skipped. To test: sign up with a code that gives bonus tokens on a subscription, pay, and check the balance includes them (trial carry-over tokens + the plan's monthly tokens + the plan's sign-up bonus + the code's tokens); a second purchase should not give them again.

entries.summary: Admin: the tiers' Sign-up bonus setting reminds you that people also keep their Free Trial carry-over tokens.
entries.detail: Dashboard, Tiers and Passes.

entries.summary: A discount code you enter when you sign up is now applied for you at checkout.
entries.detail: When you go on to buy a subscription, a pass or tokens that your sign-up code covers, the checkout opens with the discount already applied. If the code cannot be used on that purchase (for example it is for first purchases only), the checkout opens as before and you can still enter a code there. To test: make a discount code for a subscription tier, sign up with it from that tier's button on the home page, confirm the email, and check the Stripe checkout shows the discount; sign up with a code for a different product and check the checkout is full price with the code box; use the code once and check a second purchase does not get it again.

entries.summary: Sign-up now tells you when a promo code is used up, expired or switched off, instead of ignoring it.
entries.detail: The message appears by Create Account and the promo code box is highlighted; remove the code or enter another to continue. A code we do not recognise is still accepted as before. To test: sign up with a used-up code, an expired code and a switched-off code (each should stop with its reason, no account made); clear the box and sign up normally; a working tester code still makes a tester.

entries.summary: Admin and testers: promo codes that can no longer be used say Used up or Expired in the list; Set exact says the 1000 tester limit before sending.
entries.detail: Promo Codes list: a code that is on but past its expiry or out of uses shows Expired or Used up in red. Tester tools: Set exact over 1000 in total now says so at once.

entries.summary: The Library's genre and art style filters keep your choices inside the drop-down, so the page no longer jumps around.
entries.detail: Click Genre or Art style for a list with a tick box beside each choice; ticking filters at once. The button shows what is picked (for example Genre: Fantasy +2) and turns gold. Clear unticks that list; Show everything clears both. To test: tick and untick on Gallery and Books, check nothing on the row moves, Esc or a click elsewhere closes the list, a Library link with a genre already in it shows that genre on the button, and on a phone the list opens full width under its button.

entries.summary: Sign-up problems now show right by the Create Account button, and the field to fix is highlighted.
entries.detail: The field that needs fixing gets an amber outline, shakes once and is scrolled into view; fixing it clears the message. To test: on the sign-up form, leave the name empty, use a short password, leave out the date of birth, use a date under 18, leave either box unticked, use an email that already has an account and a pen name already taken -- each time the message should be by the button and the right field should shake.

entries.summary: The Library's top is much shorter, so the books and pictures start higher up.
entries.detail: The headline sits at the top left with its line beside it, and the tabs, genre and art style pickers, search (or Last 6 Months / All Time on the Gallery) and Show everything share one row under it. To test: Gallery and Books at full width, tablet and phone widths; pick a genre and an art style and check the chips and Show everything appear on the row; The Guild tab (when on) still hides the filters.

entries.summary: The Library's tabs are now called Gallery and Books.
entries.detail: Gallery holds the public pictures and Books the published stories. Links to the Library keep working. To test: both tabs switch as before, the Books search box and its empty messages say books, and the help assistant answers questions about the Library with the new names.

entries.summary: The ?s help buttons now say what they do as soon as you hover over them.
entries.detail: Hover over ?s to see: Questions? Ask us anything -- tips, how-tos, getting started. The ?s buttons in the Title Builder and on characters show their own tips the same way.

entries.summary: Testers: the badge in the top bar is now a silver Platinum Tester button.
entries.detail: It still opens the testing tools; that the account is not billed is in its tooltip.

entries.summary: Admin: Make a Tester promo codes, a Testers list, and a 1000-token cap on testers' own top-ups.
entries.detail: Promo Codes has a new type, Make a Tester (Platinum): anyone who signs up with such a code becomes a tester on Platinum and skips the payment page, up to the code's total uses. The Testers list shows them with an on/off switch, can make any existing account a tester, and lists the TESTER_EMAILS from Railway. Testers can give themselves tokens only up to a balance of 1000; tokens they buy are on top, and admins are not capped. Testers can no longer change a tier's session reserve.

entries.summary: The Library's hover card opens just above your pointer, and the blurb opens on a click.
entries.detail: The card sits just above where the pointer came onto the book, so the book stays in view. Click the blurb's first line (or its more link) to read the whole blurb over the cover; the card keeps its size. Click again to bring the cover back.

entries.summary: The Library's hover card now shows the start of each book's blurb.
entries.detail: The card shows the blurb up to its first line break, with an ellipsis when there is more. Hover over that line (tap it on a phone) to read the whole blurb in the card. A book with no blurb shows the opening of its story, as its page does.

entries.summary: The Library now lists campaigns newest first.
entries.detail: When a new book is published, its whole campaign moves to the top of the Library, all its books together in the author's order. That author's other campaigns stay where their own newest book puts them. Publishing again over a book that is already in the Library does not move it. The card shown when you hover over a book now covers the top half of the book and never goes under the menu bar.

entries.summary: Hovering over a book in the Library now shows its whole cover, bigger.
entries.detail: Books standing with their spines out show their cover too. Near the top of the window the card slides down over the book instead of being cut off.

entries.summary: The Library's stories now look like books on a bookshelf.
entries.detail: Each story stands like a book on the Bookshelf, with its pen name on a brass plate on the shelf. A campaign of three or more books shows its first and last books face out and the ones between with their spines out. Hover over a book (tap once on a phone) to see its title, subtitle, date, genres and + Bookshelf. The author search now sits on the same row as Show everything.

entries.summary: The Library's stories now stand on wooden shelves, pen names side by side.
entries.detail: Each pen name is written above its books, with a gap between pen names and a smaller one between campaigns. The + Bookshelf button is smaller and sits with the genre pills under the title instead of on the cover.

entries.summary: Members who may add assets now get + Assets on the Archive pictures too.
entries.detail: It showed for the Story Master only, though the campaign setting lets members add assets.

entries.summary: Session Characters tab: retouch several characters at once and approve each as it comes back.
entries.detail: Approving, discarding or cancelling one character used to close every other open edit and hide the retouches still running. Now only that character closes; the others keep their text, their spinner and their new picture when it arrives.

entries.summary: Dashboard, Public Library: Open Stories and Open Library have a name filter.
entries.detail: Admin only. Stories: title, pen name or campaign. Images: caption, campaign, or the name, pen name or email of whoever shared it; each image tile now says who and which campaign.

entries.summary: Dashboard, Public Library: Open Stories and Open Library show whole cards again, with their Remove buttons, and scroll to load more.
entries.detail: Admin only.

entries.summary: My Published Stories cards show the book's own cover, title and all, with the published date at the bottom.
entries.detail: The same cover the Library shows. If it cannot be drawn, the cover picture shows instead.

entries.summary: My Published Stories cards show the subtitle under the title.
entries.detail: The one the book was published with, as on the Library card.

entries.summary: In the Library, each of an author's campaigns starts its own line of books.
entries.detail: In the order the author set on My Stuff, Published Stories.

entries.summary: Put your published stories in order: My Stuff, Published Stories, grouped by pen name and campaign.
entries.detail: Drag a book (or use its arrows) to move it within its campaign, or drag a campaign to move it as a whole. The Library shows your books in that order, left to right. A campaign, or a single book, can also be moved to another of your pen names.

entries.summary: The Optimize progress now reads Editor Loop 1, Editor Loop 2 and so on.
entries.detail: Its messages speak of the editor rather than the AI.

entries.summary: On the Archive screen the filter Pin sits right after Clear filters again.
entries.detail: The picture windows keep it beside their close button.

entries.summary: The Characters page has a Back button, and its Publish button is gone.
entries.detail: Back takes you to the page you opened Characters from, or to the campaign's Sessions.

entries.summary: Prep & Preview: the Refresh preview button sits above the preview and glows when you have a change it does not show yet.
entries.detail: Change a title, picture, colour or layout setting on the Prep panel and the button wiggles once and keeps a soft glow until the preview is redrawn.

entries.summary: A Characters button at the top of Publish, beside Archives.
entries.detail: It opens the campaign's Characters page.

entries.summary: Library story cards show the book's subtitle under its title.
entries.detail: It is the subtitle the book was published with. Stories published before books kept their subtitle show none.

entries.summary: The filter pin now sits on the title row, so it never pushes the pictures down.
entries.detail: In the Archive and every picture window, the Pin button is beside the close button (or Back on the Archive screen) instead of after the filters.

entries.summary: Put your own published stories on your Bookshelf.
entries.detail: On My Stuff, Published Stories, each story has an Add to my Bookshelf button. It puts a copy of the book on your shelf as one of your own books, so it stays there even if you later unpublish or replace the story. It counts toward your Bookshelf limit.

entries.summary: My Account has a Back button.
entries.detail: It takes you back to the page you opened My Account from, or to My Campaigns if that is not known.

entries.summary: Stories in the Library now show the book's own cover, title and all, as it is in the book.
entries.detail: On the Library, on each story's page, on Library books on your Bookshelf, and in the picture shown when a story link is shared. The title and subtitle are still written out below. If a cover cannot be drawn, the cover picture shows instead.

entries.summary: Pin your picture filters. The Archive screen and every window that picks a picture from the Archive now has a Pin button that keeps your filters for next time.
entries.detail: Each place keeps its own pin, per campaign, on this computer: the Archive screen, the Replace windows for panels, characters, assets and title images, the four Prep and Preview pictures together, and the Title Builder. A pinned filter that no longer matches anything is dropped, so a pinned window never opens empty. A character's Replace window always opens on that character.

entries.summary: The character page (The Company) now shows only the characters in the sessions you put in the book, and a new Character pictures choice decides which picture of each one is used.
entries.detail: Choose from: Canonical (the original pictures of the characters), the first or last appearance in this version, or the first or last appearance in the sessions in this book, which is the new default. A book whose layout was already saved keeps the picture it had. The choice shows when Include character page is ticked.

entries.summary: Replace from Archive now opens showing your pictures, instead of an empty window that needed Clear filters.
entries.detail: For a panel it opens on this session's pictures from every version, newest first, or on the whole Archive when the session has none yet. A filter the dropdowns cannot show is never left on.

entries.summary: Getting started: an 18th step, Enjoy your book! Someone who has already published or ordered a book opens at the end, and password managers no longer offer to fill in the guide.
entries.detail: GS_STEPS gains step 18 (no Take me there). /api/help/start returns made_book. The guide's buttons carry the ignore attributes LastPass, 1Password, Bitwarden, Dashlane and Proton Pass read. Brain 1a and the getting-started instruction say 18 steps.

entries.summary: Help: once the first session exists and is Ready, a character is changed as the story goes along on that session's Characters tab (Ian).
entries.detail: Brain sections 1a, 9 and 10.2, and step 2 of the Getting started guide.

entries.summary: Help: characters are first made on the Characters screen (the Characters button); once the first session exists, they change as the story goes along on that session's Characters tab.
entries.detail: The assistant's knowledge (sections 1a, 9, 10.2, 12, 19 and the FAQ) and step 2 of the Getting started guide. Also carries the getting-started answer fix that missed v3.3.23: all 17 steps, numbered, the five publishing steps included.

entries.summary: Getting started: Show guided tours again (and the Dashboard's Clear tour history) brings the pill back until the guide is opened; asking the assistant how to get going adds an Open the step-by-step guide button under its answer.
entries.detail: Tour reset writes gs_offer into tour_progress; GET /api/help/start reports it; POST /api/help/start/seen drops it when the guide opens. /api/help/ask strips a <<GET_STARTED>> marker and returns guide:true; the pill also shows for the rest of that visit.

entries.summary: New to Campaignia? The Ask Us panel now has a Get started step by step guide.
entries.detail: Press New here? Get started step by step at the top of Ask Us for the whole path from your first campaign to a printed book, one step at a time. It opens at the step you have reached, and Take me there opens the right page. The pill goes away once you have published or ordered a book.

entries.summary: Help assistant: a Getting started section with the same 17 steps; styles are picked on the Story tab before Generate Story; moments cannot be moved or removed on Review.
entries.detail: routes/campaignia_brain.md: new section 1a; 10.1 and 10.3 corrected; the Where do I start answer points at 1a. GET /api/help/start (routes/help.js) tells the guide where the person is.

entries.summary: Landing pages: a fifth What You Get box, Better Together: invite players (or family and friends) free, make your own versions, compare them, share pictures and ideas.
entries.detail: The home page, /game-masters and /story, each worded for its page.

entries.summary: Landing pages: Write It Yourself now says "The GM who keeps a campaign journal?" (was DM).
entries.detail: The home page and /game-masters.

entries.summary: Landing pages: the Multiple Layout Styles box is now Total Creative Control: all the tools in one place to edit every part of your book (rewrite the narrative, retouch images, rework the layout).
entries.detail: The home page, /game-masters and /story.

entries.summary: Landing pages: the line under the trial offer now says Print-ready PDF or full hardcover graphic novel (was Print-ready PDF export).
entries.detail: The home page, /game-masters and /story.

entries.summary: The Guild (still switched off): fixes from the test run before it is parked.
entries.detail: A paused listing now says only that it is paused (it also said Live). Saving names any link left out because it is not a web address. A listing with no pictures shows no empty picture slot. The contact email prints a name once when name and pen name match. The approval email links to the listing. The one-message refusal says "in the last 24 hours". The Guild Terms say Campaignia does not vet anyone listed (still version 1.0).

entries.summary: Story landing page: "your family" is now "your characters" in the steps and the features.
entries.detail: views/story.html: the reference-pictures step and the visual-consistency feature line.

entries.summary: The Marketplace (still switched off) is now The Guild: "Artists, writers and Campaignia Specialists you can hire."
entries.detail: Renamed everywhere it shows: the Library tab (now with a heading and that subtitle), the user menu, My Account, the links under the story box and on the art brief, the listing editor, the emails, the Dashboard switch and review window. Its pages moved to /guild and /guild/<name>-<number>; the old /marketplace addresses forward. The Marketplace Terms are now the Guild Terms at /guild-terms.html, same wording and still version 1.0, so nobody has to accept them again.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): "Campaignia Editors" is now "Campaignia Specialists": people who build a whole book in Campaignia for you.
entries.detail: Renamed everywhere it shows: the Library filter, the introductions, the listing editor (each kind of help now has a one-line explanation beside it), card and page tags, the Marketplace page's search description and the Marketplace Terms. Listings that had ticked it keep it.

entries.summary: Marketplace review window (still switched off): opens on a new filter, Needing attention, showing every listing waiting for review and every live listing altered since it was approved.
entries.detail: The other filters are unchanged. With nothing to look at it says Nothing needs your attention.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): a Share button on each artist's page, like the one on published stories, in place of Copy link.
entries.detail: On a phone it opens the phone's own share sheet; on a computer it copies the link and says Link copied. The listing editor's page link has the same Share.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): a Back button on each artist's page, back to wherever they came from.
entries.detail: From the app, the Library's Marketplace tab or the Marketplace page it steps back there (and says where: Back to Campaignia, Back to the Library, Back to the Marketplace). Arriving from outside, such as a search result or a shared link, it goes to the Marketplace page; in a tab opened from the app it goes to the app.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): the sample pictures on an artist's page, and the picture on each Marketplace card, are shown whole, never cropped.
entries.detail: On the page, the first picture runs the full width and the rest sit two to a row, each at its own shape; a very tall one is shrunk to fit the screen rather than cut. Cards keep one size and show the whole picture with dark bands where its shape differs.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): artists say how they make their art (Traditional, Digital, 3D, AI-generated, AI-assisted, plus a line in their own words), and watermarked or signed samples are shown to Campaignia for review instead of being refused.
entries.detail: The medium shows as tags on the cards and pages, with AI work labelled plainly; it is asked only of listings that offer art, and at least one box must be ticked to send for review. Sample pictures still get the free watermark and signature check, but its answer only goes to the review window, because artists often mark their own portfolios. The 800-pixel minimum stays.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): clicking a card on the Library's Marketplace tab opens that person's own page, and the Make contact form is on the page itself.
entries.detail: The page shows the form to a signed-in visitor, a Sign in to make contact button to others, and an Edit it link to the listing's owner. It is filled in after the page loads, so the page can still be cached for everyone.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): every live listing has its own page that search engines can read, plus a Marketplace page listing everyone, and both are in the sitemap.
entries.detail: /marketplace/<name>-<number> carries the listing's title, description, share preview picture and structured data, built on the server; a renamed listing's old address forwards to the new one. /marketplace lists every live listing as links. While the switch is off both answer 404 except to admins (marked noindex), and the Marketplace sitemap is empty. The listing window and the editor show the page's address with Copy link, so artists can share it.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): its own Marketplace Terms page, a tick box in the listing editor, and a line on Make contact.
entries.detail: The page is /marketplace-terms.html (version 1.0), linked only from the editor and the contact form; the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are unchanged until launch. Send for review and Update my listing need the box ticked once per Terms version (date and version kept on the listing); pressing them unticked shakes the box. Save draft does not need it.

entries.summary: Replying to a Campaignia email that names someone to reply to (feedback, email-change notices, content reports, order problem reports) now reaches them.
entries.detail: The reply address was set in a form the email service ignores, so replies went to Campaignia's sending address instead. Every email that names someone to reply to now uses it.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): once a listing has been approved, its edits go live at once and show in the review window as Altered; listing and making contact need a confirmed email.
entries.detail: Update my listing publishes straight away for an approved listing; support is emailed that a live listing changed. The review window has an Altered (already live) filter, lists what changed since approval, and offers Accept changes or Send back, which puts the approved version back up. A listing never approved still waits for review.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): sample pictures must be at least 800 pixels on the longer side; the picture viewer enlarges a picture to at most twice its real size; the user menu's Marketplace item matches the others and shows only once the Marketplace is on.
entries.detail: A smaller sample is refused before anything is stored or checked, with its size in the message. Shown full screen, small pictures had been stretched until they looked soft and blocky; big pictures still shrink to fit the screen.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): up to 10 sample pictures, several chosen at once; and a Back to review button in the review window.
entries.detail: Choose several pictures in one go: they upload one after another through the usual watermark check, stop at 10, and a line says how many were added, which look signed and which were refused. Back to review (admin) puts any listing that is not waiting back into Waiting for review and takes it off the Marketplace, emailing nobody, so the approval can be tried again.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): support gets an email whenever a listing is sent for review, new or changed.
entries.detail: Sent to SUPPORT_EMAIL (support@campaignia.com unless set), with the person's name, email, headline, what they offer, how many sample pictures, and how many listings are waiting in all. Reply goes to the person. A plain Save draft sends nothing.

entries.summary: Marketplace (still switched off): bigger text in the review window, one plain label under each sample picture, and a line saying whose name is signed on the pictures beside the account's name.
entries.detail: The app's own picture marker no longer adds its outline and sentence on top of the review window's pictures (that squeezed the row). A listing with no signatures says so, and that the check can't recognise well-known art. Clicking a sample (in the review window, the editor, or a listing on the Library tab) now opens it filling the screen instead of the file at its own small size.

entries.summary: Artist Marketplace, stage one (switched off): a Library tab where artists, writers and Campaignia editors list themselves, Make contact by email, and a review window on the Dashboard.
entries.detail: Off until launch (Dashboard > Settings > Marketplace); while it is off only admins see the Library tab, the links in the app and the listing section in My Account. A listing appears only after it is approved; editing an approved listing sends the changes for review while the approved copy stays up. Make contact emails the person listed with the sender's address to reply to; nobody's email is shown on a page. Sample pictures get the same watermark check as every upload. Spec: claude/ARTIST_MARKETPLACE_SPEC.md.

entries.summary: Landing pages load the current stylesheet, so a browser that had the old one cached shows the book photo window properly.
entries.detail: 3.3.00 added the photo window's styles to landing.css without changing the version number the pages ask for, so a cached copy left the photos unstyled until a refresh.

entries.summary: Home, Game Masters and Storyteller pages: “See what they look like” under A REAL BOOK opens photos of real printed Campaignia books.
entries.detail: Ten photographs of books made with Campaignia and printed for their owners (covers and inside pages), one large at a time with arrows and thumbnails. The Storyteller page opens on a family story, the Game Masters page on the fantasy books.

entries.summary: Calm & Literal narrative style: its example says “Mom”, not “Mum”.
entries.detail: The style card, the example the writer follows, and the help assistant's sample all say Mom now.

entries.summary: Printed books: the note on the details page now reads “the creators’ stories” (the apostrophe was missing).
entries.detail: Books saved or ordered from now on carry the corrected note. Books already saved keep the old wording until they are optimized and saved again.

entries.summary: Home, Game Masters and Storyteller pages: the FAQ now answers “Is my work safe with AI?”
entries.detail: It replaces “Do I need my own AI API keys?”: the AI is built in with nothing to set up, and neither Campaignia nor our AI providers ever train AI models on your stories or art. The help assistant gives the same answer, and names the providers if asked.

entries.summary: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy 1.3: we never use your stories or pictures to train AI, and our AI providers' terms with us forbid it too.
entries.detail: Terms section 4 gains a No AI training paragraph, and Privacy Policy section 3 says the same in plain words. If a provider ever changed its terms, we would move to one that keeps this promise. Both pages are now version 1.3, dated October 27, 2026.

entries.summary: Writing Coach: shorter wording on the Feedback tab and in the Story tour.
entries.detail: The Feedback tab on a narrative box now says “Get honest feedback — hit the button below.” The Story tour's Writing Coach step says 4 uses per token.

entries.summary: A long campaign or session name no longer pushes the buttons beside it onto another line.
entries.detail: On a wide screen the name stays on one line and ends with …, with the buttons kept on the right; hover the name to read all of it. On a phone the name uses at most two lines. Editing the name still shows the whole of it.

entries.summary: Publish to Library: pressing Publish without ticking the rights box now lights up the box and scrolls to it, instead of a small line under the button.
entries.detail: The “I own or have the rights to this content” row is outlined in amber, shakes once and scrolls into view, and the line under the button says which box to tick. Ticking it clears both. The Publish as window and the replace messages no longer mention the Bookshelf; they say a replaced story keeps its link and its place in the Library.

entries.summary: Publish as: bigger book cards with just the cover, and A new story sits beside your book.
entries.detail: Each card in the Publish as window now shows only the front cover, large and upright, with the title, subtitle, sessions and date underneath. Your book and A new story share the top row; the stories you could replace are in a grid below. Two cards a row on a phone. Choosing works exactly as before.

entries.summary: Storyboard: a picture that is regenerating or being retouched keeps its spinner while you work on other pictures, and can't be started twice by mistake.
entries.detail: The spinner used to vanish whenever the Storyboard redrew (another picture landing, a tweak, a dialog closing), though the picture was still being drawn; pressing Regen again then paid for a second picture that replaced the first. Now the spinner stays until the picture lands, sits in the middle of the picture rather than the middle of the whole card, and comes back after a page refresh. While it runs, Regen, Retouch, Replace and Revert on that picture are greyed and say it is still being worked on, and the server refuses a second job on the same picture without charging. Test: Regen one picture, then Retouch or Regen another and open a dialog; the first keeps its spinner and its new picture appears once.

entries.summary: Publishing again from a campaign: “Publish as” is now a picture picker. Each published book shows its cover, title, subtitle and title-page picture, with your book at the top to compare.
entries.detail: Order & Publish > Publish as opens a window: your book (cover, title, subtitle, title picture) at the top, then A new story and one card per story already published from this campaign, with its cover, title, subtitle, title-page picture, sessions, date and link only. Choosing a card works exactly as the old list did (same note, link only and blurb behaviour). Stories published before their subtitle and title picture were recorded show the cover and title only. Test: on a campaign with two or more published stories, open Publish as, pick one, then pick A new story.

entries.summary: Making a second version without Gold now shows a plain “More versions need Gold” box with Upgrade My Plan, instead of “Something went wrong.”
entries.detail: The message itself was right, but it sat under an error heading and read like a crash. It now uses the same box as the other plan limits (like the Title Builder): a heading that names the limit, the same sentence, a note that nothing you made is affected, and Upgrade My Plan / Not now. Both ways of making a version (New Version and Make My Version) show it. Test: as a Copper member with one version already, try to make another.

entries.summary: Dashboard > Stats: a slider between the stats and the users grid.
entries.detail: Drag the bar between the two to make either side wider; it lets go when you release, like the Prep & Preview slider, and the width is remembered in this browser. On a narrow screen the two still stack with no slider. Test: Dashboard > Stats, drag the bar, release, reload.

entries.summary: After using the slider on Prep & Preview, the mouse wheel scrolls the preview again straight away.
entries.detail: v3.2.86 fixed the slider letting go by switching the preview frame off during the drag; switching it back on left the mouse wheel dead over Quick View until its scrollbar was dragged. The preview is no longer touched: while you drag, an invisible sheet covers the page and is removed when you let go. The slider still lets go on release. Same on the Optimize slider. Test: drag the slider, let go over the preview, then scroll it with the wheel.

entries.summary: The slider between the Prep panel and the preview now lets go when you release the mouse; no second click needed. Same for the Optimize tab slider.
entries.detail: Releasing the mouse over the preview was never heard by the page (the preview is a separate frame), so the slider stayed stuck to the pointer until the next click. While you drag, the preview now ignores the pointer, and a move with no button held or the window losing focus also ends the drag. Test: on Prep & Preview, drag the slider over the preview and let go.

entries.summary: On the page after the title page, the copyright line, the Campaignia logo and the notice sit lower, nearer the foot of the page.
entries.detail: The bottom padding of the details page went from 1 inch to 0.4 inch, so the footer block (copyright line, logo, notice) moves down about 0.6 inch. Still well inside the printed page margins. Test: preview a book and look at page 3.

entries.summary: The Title, Subtitle and Author’s Note boxes now save as you type, and an edit is kept even if you refresh or close the page straight away.
entries.detail: They used to save only when you clicked out of the box, so a refresh with the cursor still in it lost the edit. Now each saves about a second after you stop typing, and anything not yet saved is sent as the page closes, refreshes or goes to the background. An emptied Title is not saved while you retype it; leaving the box still puts the campaign name back. Test: type in each box and refresh at once; type and wait two seconds, then refresh.

entries.summary: The copyright line on the page after the title page now sits at the bottom, just above the Campaignia logo.
entries.detail: On the details page (page 3), the line © year name. All rights reserved. moved from under Players and Story Master (and the Author’s Note) down to the foot of the page, directly above the Campaignia logo and notice. Test: preview any book and look at page 3.

entries.summary: Your subtitle now prints under the title on the title page and on the page after it, as well as on the cover. That page no longer prints the campaign name.
entries.detail: Pages 2 and 3 of the book (the title page with its picture, and the page with the copyright notice) show the subtitle in small italics under the title, the same words as the cover. The campaign name is no longer printed on page 3; it may only be a working name, and shows only if you put it in the title or subtitle. No subtitle, nothing extra. Test: preview a book with and without a subtitle.

entries.summary: New Author’s Note box under the Subtitle: a note, message or dedication to your readers, printed on the page after the title page.
entries.detail: Order & Publish > Title & Cover: up to 600 characters with a counter, line breaks kept, no heading added. It prints on page 3 (the page with the copyright notice), below Players and Story Master and above the copyright line, in the PDF and the printed book only (not the Library page). Saved per version with the title, subtitle and cover, and kept with a saved book, so an ordered or reloaded book prints the note it was saved with; changing it after a save shows as a title and cover change. Test: type a note, preview, save the book, change the note, reload the saved book.

entries.summary: A camera date stamp on an uploaded picture (like 11/16/2006 in the corner) no longer counts as a watermark.
entries.detail: The picture check sometimes reported a camera date stamp as a watermark and refused the picture. If the only text it reads is a date and/or time, the picture is no longer refused; a watermark with any words, a name, a web address or a stock mark beside or instead of the date still is. Covers uploads, character reference builds and custom art style Analyze. Pictures already refused stay as they are (Ian). Test: upload a snapshot with an orange camera date stamp as an asset.

entries.summary: Two new narrative styles: How To / Self Help / Instructional (Gold) and News Report (Silver). Both follow your story closely and keep your numbered steps and bullet points as lists.
entries.detail: How To writes clear, practical instruction to the reader as you, in your steps and your order, and never adds steps or advice. News Report writes a factual report: most important facts first, short paragraphs, third person, past tense, quoting only what people actually said. Test: pick each in the Narrative style window (How To shows Gold only below Gold), Generate Narrative on a story with numbered steps, and check the lists come through.

entries.summary: Two new genres: How To / Self Help / Instructional and News Report. Each starts on its own narrative style and on Everyday life art (change either any time), with its own examples in the story boxes. News Report stories publish link only by default, like Family Stories.
entries.detail: Both are nonfiction. How To defaults to the How To style (Gold; Classic below Gold) and News Report to the News Report style (Silver; Classic on Copper); both default to Everyday life illustration. News Report is sensitive: link-only publishing, the confirm before going public, Story Master only for public images. The Library genre filter lists both. Brain updated (8b, 8c, 8d, FAQ) and its sensitive-genre lines now name Biography too. Test: new campaign with each genre; check the example text in the Story and Story Instructions boxes and the character Role field, the default styles, and that a News Report publishes link only.

entries.summary: With Already Written, the narrative buttons now say Place Narrative instead of Generate Narrative, because your own words are placed beside the pictures, not written for you.
entries.detail: Labels only; what the buttons do is unchanged. Review tab: Campaignia draws + Already Written reads Place Narrative, Generate Images; I'll illustrate it myself + Already Written reads Place Narrative; I'll illustrate it myself with any other style still reads Generate Narrative; otherwise Generate Narrative & Images. Storyboard: Place Narrative with Already Written, else Generate Narrative, and while it runs it says Placing narrative. The labels change as soon as the narrative style or who draws changes. Test: switch a version between Already Written and another style, and the illustrate switch, and read both tabs.

entries.summary: Members working on their own version now see the Narrative and Art style buttons on the Story tab, beside Generate Story, as the Story Master does.
entries.detail: The Story tab's Narrative and Art style buttons (added in v3.1.51) were left off the style-sheet lists that show a member's own-version controls and hide them on someone else's version, so a member saw Generate Story alone. Both lists now name them. Test as a member on your own version: Story tab shows Narrative, Art and Generate Story; on another person's version none of the three show.

entries.summary: Already Written: Generate Story now puts the pictures in the order your text tells them and spreads them across the whole story, so every picture gets its own words and long passages are not left without a picture.
entries.detail: With Already Written chosen as the narrative style, Generate Story asks for the pictures in the order their passages appear in the text (not the order the events happened), spread from start to end, each with the first words of its passage; the server then sorts the pictures into text order by those words, so a reply that ignores the request is still put right. Every other narrative style is unchanged. Railway log line: [written-order] ... N of M panels found in the text; reordered to ... Test: on Salmon River Trip, choose Already Written, Generate Story, then Generate Narrative; no picture should be left with no text, and no long run of text should sit under one picture.

entries.summary: Manage holding bucket: the results line is bigger and bolder.
entries.detail: Dashboard > Tools > Monthly clean-up > Manage holding bucket: the line under the buttons (Check holding, Put back, Delete for good results and progress) is larger, bold and gold, like the Results line above. Test: press Check holding.

entries.summary: Monthly clean-up: the per-folder result line and the running count are bigger and bolder.
entries.detail: Dashboard > Tools > Monthly clean-up: the per-folder line under Last run now starts with "Results:" and, like the "Running: ... N of M" line while it works, is larger, bold and gold. Test: press Run report and read the Results line.

entries.summary: The monthly clean-up and Move to holding cover PDFs and saved books too, not just pictures.
entries.detail: Monthly clean-up, Run report and Move to holding now handle every folder: pictures, archived pictures, saved books / Bookshelf copies / order covers and published story PDFs over 30 days old, and print PDFs over 90. Held files keep their folder (production/print/... etc.), so Put back returns each to the right place; a bare name is looked up in every folder. Brakes: nothing moves if over 60% of the whole bucket looks orphaned, and a folder where over 85% looks orphaned (at least 10 files) is left alone that run. Holding, the held list and the email show a line per folder. The Monthly job toggle stays as it was (Off). Test: on staging Run report and Check holding; on production Run report, then Move to holding once, then Check holding.

entries.summary: Orphaned pictures and PDFs: the read-only check now covers every storage folder.
entries.detail: Dashboard > Tools > Orphaned pictures and PDFs (read only): Check for orphaned pictures and PDFs lists every folder (Pictures uploads/, Archived pictures archives/, Saved books / Bookshelf copies / order covers optimized/, Published story PDFs story/, Print PDFs print/) with files, size, in use, too new and orphaned, then the oldest 200 orphans with their folder; the CSV has a folder column. Same check as before (database plus saved books). Print PDFs younger than 90 days are left out (an order waits in the browser until paid); everything else younger than a day. Moves nothing; the monthly clean-up still handles pictures only. Test: on production, press the button and read the folder table.

entries.summary: Dashboard Tools: the storage panels reworded so every button says what it does; the staging move tool removed.
entries.detail: Orphaned pictures (read only): Check for orphaned pictures. Monthly clean-up: a Monthly job On/Off toggle (On moves orphaned pictures over 30 days to holding on the 1st and deletes what has been held over 90 days; Off only emails the report), Run report, Move to holding. Manage holding bucket: Check holding, Download the held list, Put back (one per line or commas), Put back anything no longer orphaned, Put back everything, Delete from holding [age] Delete for good; a description beside every button. Move to its own storage (staging, one time) is removed with its routes and services/storageMove.js. Test: on staging, open Tools and read each panel; flip the toggle On and Off and watch the status line.

entries.summary: Dashboard: a Tools tab ; Image Generation Model removed (always Nano).
entries.detail: Dashboard has a new Tools tab (after Support). Moved there: Maintenance (weekly snapshot) and Pass expiry sweep and Email preview / test-send from Settings; Move to its own storage, Unused pictures and Monthly clean-up (now its own panel, with Holding) from Support. Nothing else changed. Image Generation Model is removed: every picture uses Nano (the FAL_IMAGE_MODEL / FAL_IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL Railway variables); the old setting is no longer read and Flux schnell is retired. Test: open each panel on Tools and press its safe button (Run the check, Check holding, Dry run, Send test to me).

entries.summary: The unused-picture check opens saved books; Put back anything now in use.
entries.detail: Saved books (Optimize saves and Bookshelf copies, optimized/approved-*.json.gz) list their panel pictures as saved; publishing, Edit and the print fallback read them. The check now opens every saved book the database mentions and counts every picture inside as in use (if one cannot be read, the check fails and nothing moves). Dashboard > Support > Holding: Put back anything now in use runs the check and puts back every held picture it finds. The report's first line says how many saved books were opened. Test: on production, Run the check (saved books opened > 0), then Put back anything now in use, and read the Last put back line.

entries.summary: The storage clean-up moves unused pictures to a holding bucket instead of deleting them.
entries.detail: Dashboard > Support > Unused pictures: the mode Delete is now Move to holding (Delete now became Move to holding now, click twice). Pictures are copied to campaignia-holding under production/ or staging/, the copy is checked, then removed from the main bucket. Holding: Check holding, Download the held list, Put back (names or addresses, one per line; never moved again), Put everything back (click twice), Empty holding (everything, or held 7+ / 30+ days; click twice). In Move to holding mode the monthly run also deletes for good anything held over 90 days, and its email says how many; in Report mode it changes nothing. Needs the campaignia-holding bucket and both R2 tokens covering it. Test on staging: Check holding (0); on production, Move to holding now, then open a moved picture (broken), Put back its address, and check it shows again.

entries.summary: Monthly storage clean-up: pictures nothing uses, over 30 days old (report only until switched to Delete).
entries.detail: Dashboard > Support > Unused pictures > Monthly clean-up: mode Off / Report only / Delete, Run report now, Delete now (click twice). Once a month (the 1st, from 09:00 UTC) it checks this environment's own bucket; Report only emails a summary, Delete removes them after one last check. Refused unless the environment is on its own bucket, or when over 60% looks unused. History (finished image jobs, debug logs, watermark checks) no longer counts as use, in the report too. Test: on staging, Run report now; on production, Run report now and read the numbers before switching to Delete.

entries.summary: Staging can move to its own storage bucket; production is unchanged.
entries.detail: The bucket name is now the Railway setting R2_BUCKET (unset = chronicle-images, as before). Dashboard > Support has a one-time staging tool: 1. Copy pictures (every picture staging's database uses, copied into its own bucket, nothing deleted), 2. Rewrite addresses (only after a clean copy). It refuses to run unless R2_BUCKET, R2_SHARED_BUCKET, R2_PUBLIC_URL and R2_LEGACY_PUBLIC_URLS are set. Test: on staging with the settings in place, Check setup, Copy, then Rewrite; old campaigns' pictures still show.

entries.summary: A panel Retouch now deletes its working files (the marker copy and the cropped tile) when it finishes.
entries.detail: They were only for the image model and were never deleted: about 116 a month. Deleted when the job ends, done or failed. Test: Retouch a panel with markers on staging; the Railway log shows "R2 deleted: 204 uploads/marked-..." when the new picture lands, and the panel looks right.

entries.summary: Dashboard > Support: a read-only report of pictures in storage that nothing points to.
entries.detail: Lists every picture under uploads/ in the bucket, reads every text column of every table in this environment's database, and shows the ones mentioned nowhere (older than 24 hours), with sizes and a CSV. Deletes nothing. Staging and production share the bucket, so only a picture unused on both is safe to delete. Test: Run the check on staging and on production; download both CSVs.

entries.summary: Dashboard > Support: Send to support emails a user's debug log without them doing anything.
entries.detail: Same email as the user's own Send to support button, marked "(sent by support)" with the admin's email in it. Test: enter a tester's email, Send to support; support@campaignia.com gets the log.

entries.summary: Dashboard > Support: turn Debug Mode on or off for a user by email.
entries.detail: An email field with Turn on, Turn off and Check. Their actions are recorded from their next one (the request recorder now also reads the setting from the database, at most once a minute per user); signing out still turns it off. Test: turn it on for a tester, have them do something, sign in as them and open the Debug panel on their Account page; the entries are there.

entries.summary: Admin shortcut: seven clicks just right of the account button turn Debug Mode on or off.
entries.detail: An invisible spot in the top banner, right of the account button. Admin accounts only; it does nothing for anyone else. A toast says ON or OFF, and the Account page box follows. Test: as admin, click the spot seven times quickly: "Debug Mode is ON."; seven more: OFF.

entries.summary: Dashboard Stats user list readable: light text on its own dark background.
entries.detail: The rows were black on dark brown. The list box now sets a dark background, light text and dark scrollbars. Test: Dashboard > Stats, the table reads clearly.

entries.summary: Dashboard Stats shows the vuuserlastactive view beside the stats.
entries.detail: Every column of the view, in its order, up to 500 rows, in a scrolling box to the right of the stats (below them on a narrow screen). Dates show as local date and time. If the view does not exist in that database, the box says so. Test: open Dashboard > Stats on staging; the list shows; on a database without the view, it says the view is not there.

entries.summary: The rights line and the save line on the Story tab run the full width, one under the other.
entries.detail: The "Only paste content you own..." line moved out of the story column to below both boxes, with "Your story and notes save automatically..." tight under it. Test: on the Story tab, both lines span the page under the two boxes.

entries.summary: Removed the hint line under Story Notes and Instructions.
entries.detail: The grey example text inside the box already says it. Test: the Story tab shows no line under the notes box's word count.

entries.summary: Regen and Feedback share the transcript cache with Generate Story and Generate Narrative.
entries.detail: When they read the whole story (up to 40,000 characters for Regen, 24,000 for Feedback), Regen and Feedback now send the same kept transcript block at the front of their instructions, so the first one after Generate Narrative reads it from the cache. Never dearer than before. Test: Generate Narrative, then Regen a box within five minutes; that writing_uses row shows cache_read_tokens about the size of the transcript.

entries.summary: The story box shows its word and character count on the Writing Coach line.
entries.detail: Under the Story / Session Transcript box, the count now sits on the same line as the Writing Coach button and shows characters as well as words.

entries.summary: Generate Story, the character-change check and Generate Narrative share the transcript through Anthropic's cache.
entries.detail: The session transcript now goes first in all three requests, word for word the same, marked to be kept five minutes; each call's own instructions follow unchanged. The change check (seconds after Generate Story) reads it at a tenth of the price, and so does Generate Narrative within five minutes of Generate Story. Already Written unchanged. Railway logs a [story cache] line per call. Test: on a test campaign, Generate Story then Generate Narrative within five minutes; logs show write on generate-story and read on change-check and generate-narrative; compare panels and prose with a run from before.

entries.summary: The Writing Coach reuses what it has already read, so a run of coach calls costs less.
entries.detail: Each coach call sends the campaign, the session and (when short enough) the whole original story first, marked for Anthropic to keep for five minutes; the box, the passage and the instructions follow. A second call within five minutes reads the kept part at a tenth of the price. Feedback, Show me and Story Feedback share one system line; Regen keeps its own. Prompts are the same words, reordered. writing_uses now logs cache_write_tokens and cache_read_tokens. Test on staging: Feedback on one box, then on the next box within five minutes; the second row in writing_uses should show cache_read_tokens above zero (if the background and story are over about 1,000 tokens).

entries.summary: New landing page for Game Masters at campaignia.com/game-masters.
entries.detail: A copy of the home page with its own address, so it can be linked and advertised to Game Masters and later get its own wording. Search engines are told it is the Game Masters page, and it is in the site map. The home page is unchanged. Test: open /game-masters (same page as the home page, tab title starts "Campaignia for Game Masters"); Compare the Tiers and the sign-up buttons work from it; /sitemap-pages.xml lists it.

entries.summary: Comic-page styles: the page behind the panels is now always black, never white. "What the questions missed" is always the last question.
entries.detail: A comic-page preview left white paper showing below its hero panel. The comic page rule now says any space not covered by a panel is solid black and the panels tile the whole picture. Test: regenerate the Group preview of a style with Comic paneling answered; no white anywhere.

entries.summary: Custom art styles can now draw every picture as a comic page with panels inside it, and allow hand-drawn sound effects.
entries.detail: Two new questions in the custom style builder. Comic paneling: none (one picture, as before) or a panel layout; any layout gives black gutters only, the same character looking the same in every panel, and no captions, titles or speech balloons. Sound effects: none, or bold hand-drawn sound effects (BOOM, CRACK) with no other text. They are read from the saved answers whenever a picture is drawn. The Soft / faded edges box is gone; soft edges follow the Edges and framing answer. Styles without these answers draw exactly as before. Test: on a custom style, answer Comic paneling ("a comic page of 4 panels, one large") and Sound effects ("none"), Rewrite, generate the three previews (black gutters, no lettering); then Sound effects "bold red sound effects" and generate again; check an existing style's previews are unchanged.

entries.summary: Custom art styles: make one by answering the 18 questions yourself, with grey examples showing what to write. The questions now fold away.
entries.detail: Reference images are optional. Each empty question shows an example answer in grey, and the same example sits in the box when you edit it. Answer at least 3 and click Rewrite descriptions (free) for the three descriptions; previews and picking a winner work as before. The questions sit in a panel that opens and shuts from its title: open on a new style, shut when you reopen one with answers (it then says how many are answered). Analyze asks first if it would replace answers you typed. Test: New style, name it, no pictures; check the grey examples; answer 3 or more; Rewrite descriptions; generate a preview; Use this one; save; reopen (panel shut, "N of 18 answered"); open it; type an answer, then Analyze with pictures (it asks).

entries.summary: The Members page heading is now the same size as the other page headings.
entries.detail: "Current Members" uses the same heading style as the Sessions page title (gold, display font, full size), with the description beside it. Test: open a campaign's Members page and compare with its Sessions page.

entries.summary: Help now gets right who counts toward a campaign's members limit: Free Trial members count, and nobody is ever removed.
entries.detail: Testers found Help calling the Free Trial "a paid plan", saying free players could join a plan whose limit is none, and saying a member would have to be removed. Help's live tier line and the Help notes now say: Copper and Free Trial members count; only a member's own Silver, Gold or Platinum subscription or a live pass doesn't; a plan set to none takes no free players; nobody is removed. Test: with Silver at 0, ask Help "Can free players join my Silver campaign?" (answer: no, they need their own paid plan or you need a higher plan) and "Does a Free Trial member count?" (yes).

entries.summary: Node.js pinned to 22.23.4, the patched release for the October Brotli security flaw (CVE-2026-111497).
entries.detail: Railway had been reusing Node 22.23.3. package.json now names 22.23.4 under engines, so every build installs it, and the start-up log prints the Node version under "Campaignia is running!". Test: staging Deploy Logs show "Node: v22.23.4"; the app works as before (sign in, open a storyboard, a Regen, a PDF preview). Production picks it up with the next promote.

entries.summary: Help now knows each plan's live members number, and Compare the Tiers shows a cross for a plan set to none.
entries.detail: The Help assistant reads "non-paying members per campaign" for every plan from the dashboard settings, the same way it reads campaigns and archives, and answers "how many members can I have" with it. In Compare the Tiers the Non-Paying Members per Campaign row shows a cross for a plan set to 0, a number otherwise, and Unlimited when blank. Test: set Silver to 0 on the dashboard and open Compare the Tiers (Silver shows a cross); ask Help "how many members can I have on Silver?"; set it back.

entries.summary: The Members page starts right under the top banner.
entries.detail: The big "Members" title is gone (the breadcrumb already says it), and "Who's in this campaign and what character they play" sits on the Current members line. Test: open a campaign's Members page, wide and on a phone.

entries.summary: Each plan now allows a set number of members per campaign who are not on a paid plan of their own. Members with their own paid plan never count.
entries.detail: Silver 6, Gold 10, Platinum 15 to start (dashboard: Tiers and Passes, "Max non-paying members / campaign", blank = unlimited). Invites waiting count; expired ones do not until reactivated. When full, inviting another non-paying member is refused with a clear message; someone with their own paid plan can always be invited. Nobody is removed from a campaign already over the number. The Story Master sees "Members not on a paid plan of their own: 4 of 10" on the Members screen, and Compare the Tiers has a row for it. Test: on staging set Silver to 1 on the dashboard, invite one Copper address (works), invite a second (refused), invite a paid account (works), revoke the first and invite again (works); open a full campaign's invite as a Copper account ("full").

entries.summary: Landing page wording tidied, and Compare the Tiers now has a Your Own Art and Narrative row.
entries.detail: Both landing pages: "AI Image Generation" is now "Image Generation"; the Narrative Prose card says Campaignia turns your session (or story) into a graphic novel, instead of talking about panels; "Artist, writer, or neither" moved up into the Play / Tell It Your Way banner. Compare the Tiers: a Your Own Art and Narrative row near the top with a tick on every plan; the Writing Coach row moved down after Multiple Versions with a cross for Silver; the footnote about your own art is gone. Test: both landing pages wide and narrow; open Compare the Tiers on each.

entries.summary: The landing pages and Compare the Tiers now show the Writing Coach, and say you can use your own art or words.
entries.detail: Both landing pages: the line under the Start buttons reads "Your own art or words, if you like"; the Arsenal strip has a fifth card, Writing Coach; Gold and Platinum list "writing coach". Compare the Tiers has a Writing Coach row (Silver: Regen only; Gold and Platinum: a tick, read from the same rule the coach uses) and a footnote: on every plan you can put your own art in the book or write it yourself. Test: open the home page and the storyteller page, wide and narrow (five cards; two with the coach across the bottom; one); open Compare the Tiers on each.

entries.summary: The Storyboard and Story tours now show the Writing Coach, and the Help assistant knows all about it.
entries.detail: The Storyboard tour has a Writing Coach step after the Narrative step, and the Narrative step no longer mentions Feedback under the box. The Story tour has a Writing Coach step after the Story box, for the Story Master. Help can now answer questions about the coach: where it is, what each tool does, Story box Feedback, plans and cost. Test: run the Storyboard tour (Narrative, then Writing Coach); run the Story tour as the Story Master (Writing Coach after Your story) and as a member (no coach step); ask Help "what does the writing coach cost?" and "what is the difference between Regen and Rewrite?".

entries.summary: The writing coach closes itself when you leave the page its box is on, and remembers where you were: press Writing Coach on the same box and your tabs are back.
entries.detail: Switch to another session tab and the coach closes; come back and press Writing Coach on the same box and its Feedback, Rewrite versions and words are still there. An answer that was still on its way lands in its tab meanwhile. Closing with × keeps them too. Moving to another session, version or campaign starts fresh. Test: Feedback on a box, switch to the Story tab (the coach closes), back to the Storyboard, Writing Coach on the same box (Feedback still there); open another session (fresh).

entries.summary: Feedback on the Story box now reads your whole story and looks at the big picture: what it is (notes, a game transcript or a written story; one chapter or the whole thing), its shape, pacing, clarity and gaps.
entries.detail: It reads the whole Story box and your Story Notes and Instructions, says what it reads as, then gives a verdict (Ready to build your book from, Close, or Needs work) with big-picture points, not line edits; transcripts are allowed to be messy. Show me is gone from the Story box; Rewrite and Word stay for working on the words. It costs one use for every 10,000 words, shown on the button. Test: a short story (1 use) and a long transcript (2+ uses on the button); the answer starts with Reads as.

entries.summary: The writing coach now knows each box's Prompt (what it should cover) and Direction (how it should be written), and you can edit both from the coach.
entries.detail: Prompt and Direction buttons sit on the coach's top line, with a tick when set; they open the same windows as the Review tab. Feedback judges whether the box covers its prompt and follows its direction (a box that misses either can't be Great) and never suggests undoing them; Show me and Rewrite stay within them. Test: set a direction on a box, then Feedback on text that ignores it (it says so); the Prompt button shows the outline Review shows.

entries.summary: Feedback now gives an honest verdict first: when your writing is truly great it says “I wouldn’t change a thing!”, when you’re close it says so with one or two small tips, and only real problems get a full list.
entries.detail: The writing coach judges each passage blind, against what a good illustrated story needs (not perfection): true to your original story, specific, in your voice, and free of stock phrases. It names what already works. The coach's Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word now look like tabs, so it is clear they switch views; the buttons inside each tab do the work. It no longer invents new tips after you have taken its earlier ones. Test: ask for Feedback on a rough box (Needs work, 3 to 5 tips); take its suggestions and ask again (Close or Great); a Great answer shows the green verdict and no tips.

entries.summary: Regen deletes the picture it no longer needs again, instead of leaving it in storage.
entries.detail: Since v3.2.21 every Regen past the first left the picture leaving the Revert slot in storage, because the panel's own note about that slot still named it when the clean-up ran. Now the slot and its note move on first, then the old picture is released. Pictures still used anywhere (archived, on another version, published) are kept as before. Test: Regen one panel three times; the log shows “R2 deleted: 204” after the second and third; Revert still brings back the previous picture with its style.

entries.summary: The Writing Coach now works on your Story / Session Transcript too: Feedback, Rewrite and Word, right under the story box.
entries.detail: Press Writing Coach under the Story box (Story Masters). Feedback reads up to about 6,000 words: the words you select, or the part around your cursor. Rewrite (all its choices) and Word work on the words you select, up to about 2,000 words at a time. Typing in the coach edits your story and saves it, as typing in the box does. Regen and Previous / Next stay with the Narrative boxes. Test: a long story, cursor near the end, Get feedback (tips about the end); select a paragraph, Rewrite > Clearer, Use this; reload the page and see the change kept.

entries.summary: The writing coach has tabs that keep their results, a wider panel, and the box name, Previous and Next on one line at the top.
entries.detail: Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word are tabs: each keeps its results while you look at the others, and clicking a tab never spends a use (each has its own start button). A tab whose results came before you edited the text says “Your text has changed since these suggestions” until you run it again. Words you select in the coach stay selected through Rewrite, and the new words are selected after Use this. Previous / Next clears the tabs, and asks first if any tab has suggestions you haven’t used. The mouse wheel over the coach scrolls only the coach. Test: Feedback, then Rewrite > Shorter on a selection, then back to Feedback (still there); edit the text (the note appears); Next with unused suggestions (asked); wheel over the coach at its end (the storyboard stays put).

entries.summary: One Writing Coach button under each Narrative box. The coach shows the box's text at the top, so you can see what you are working on wherever the box is, with every tool and Previous / Next box.
entries.detail: The row under each box is now Edit prompt, Regen, Writing Coach, Revert. The coach panel shows the box's text at the top; you can type there (it edits your story) and select words to work on just those. Below it: Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word, plus Revert. Rewrite's choices are Clearer, More vivid, More dramatic, Simpler, Add detail, Longer, Shorter, or your own way. Previous box and Next box move through the session without closing the coach. Results no longer repeat your text. Test: open the coach on the last box on the right of the page; type in the panel and see the box change; select a sentence, Rewrite > Shorter, Use this; Next box; Word on a selected word; Revert from the panel and from under the box.

entries.summary: Five new writing tools under every Narrative box: Rewrite, Describe, Expand, Tighten and Word. Select some words to work on just those, or use the whole box.
entries.detail: Rewrite offers Clearer, More vivid, More dramatic, Simpler, or your own instruction. Describe adds sight, sound and smell; Expand gives a rushed passage room; Tighten trims a wordy one. Each gives 3 versions to choose from, replaces only the words you selected (or the whole box), costs one writing use, and changes nothing until Use this. Word gives better choices for a selected word or short phrase and is free. Gold, Platinum and the Free Trial. Several Use this in a row: Revert goes back to before the first. The coach's uses line now reads like “Token: 1/4 used · 182 tokens left”. Test: select a sentence and press Rewrite > More vivid; Use this replaces only that sentence; select one word and press Word, click a choice, then another; Revert.

entries.summary: The Writing coach now knows your campaign's lore and the story so far, so Feedback and Regen stay true to your world and to what already happened.
entries.detail: Feedback, Show me and Regen now read the campaign's World / Lore and the previous session's Summary For Next Session, the same background Generate Narrative uses. They are told to stay consistent with both and not to retell them. Very long lore is trimmed for the coach (about 8,000 characters), so a use costs the same. Test: in a campaign with lore and a second session whose first session has a summary, press Feedback on a box that contradicts the lore (a wrong name or place) and see it pointed out; Regen a box and see it fit what came before.

entries.summary: Fantasy pastel is now Soft pastels, and Fantasy oil is now Oil painting. They are mediums, so they suit any kind of story.
entries.detail: New names on the art style cards, in the Library's art style filter, on Bookshelf books and in picture alt text. Nothing else changes: books and pictures already made in these styles keep them, and the pictures are drawn exactly as before. Test: open the art style picker (Soft pastels and Oil painting, same pictures and descriptions); a campaign already set to either style shows the new name; the Library art style filter lists the new names and still finds the old pictures.
